Data from XRPL explorer Bithomp reveals that the Batch and Ticket features on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) are increasingly being adopted, with both setting new daily records in November.

The data indicates an increasing use of two XRPL features intended to enhance transaction flexibility and efficiency on the network.

Batch activity reached a new daily high for the month at 1.962 million on November 3, 2026. Ticket activity came next at 1.553 million on November 7, 2026, also setting a new November record. The increase indicates that these features are being embraced in the XRPL ecosystem. Batch functionality allows multiple transactions to be grouped and executed together and was activated on the XRPL mainnet on October 9, 2026.

The growth in batch activity, which neared 2 million on November 3, 2026, comes less than one month after its launch.

This is significant, as Batch is a prerequisite or accelerant for several high-value XRPL use cases already under contract or in the active pipeline, including atomic multi-party settlements. Institutional workflows (custody transfers, DvP settlement, cross-border payment finalization) require two or more accounts to act simultaneously.

On the other hand, tickets provide a way to reserve transaction sequence numbers, giving users more flexibility in managing transactions.

XRP Ledger metrics are in the green, with the transaction count up 75.9% to 4.3 million; active accounts jumped 128%, while XRP burned as fees rose 136%. Payments volume surged 137% in the last 24 hours to $1 billion, according to XRPScan data, while NFT mints rose 240% in the same timeframe.

Not only is the XRP Ledger seeing increased activity, but Ripple led stablecoin market cap growth by issuer over the past 24 hours, up $90.9 million, 4x the next issuer, multipli.fi, at $21.3 million.

Ripple's RLUSD market cap has grown 96% this year, across Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, to $2.7 billion from $1.4 billion in January. Most of that growth came in July, when Ripple launched Ripple Mint. RLUSD market cap stood just under $1.5 billion that month and rose to $2.3 billion by August.

In a milestone for the network, one year ago today, the first US ETF to hold only XRP began trading. Since then, US spot XRP ETFs have accumulated over 1.16 billion XRP.

#5231. Vitalik Buterin Wants Crypto to Have Housing’s Stability, But Can Ethereum Deliver?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin believes younger generations investing in stocks and digital assets instead of housing could help ease pressure on property prices. However, he says crypto still needs something that makes housing attractive: stability.

Buterin thinks that housing creates incentives for owners to keep property prices high, even when cheaper homes would benefit society. Digital assets could offer an alternative, but today’s platforms often encourage excessive speculation.

“We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets,” Buterin wrote on X

His comments raise a question for Ethereum. Can the network evolve beyond speculative trading and become dependable infrastructure for people building long-term digital wealth?

One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities.That…

Ethereum’s development roadmap increasingly focuses on making the network faster, more efficient, and harder to disrupt. Its next major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is currently undergoing devnet testing, with a mainnet launch expected in Q4 2026. The upgrade introduces several changes designed to improve Ethereum’s capacity without sacrificing decentralization.

One major feature is Enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS). It moves the relationship between block proposers and builders directly into Ethereum’s protocol, reducing reliance on external relays and additional trust assumptions.

Another important development is Block-Level Access Lists. The feature prepares Ethereum to process unrelated transactions in parallel rather than handling everything sequentially.

These improvements could help Ethereum support more financial applications while keeping its infrastructure accessible to independent node operators. So, if digital assets are expected to become long-term financial instruments rather than vehicles for short-term speculation, this is very much needed.

Ethereum also provides an established foundation for staking, stablecoins, decentralized lending, and tokenized real-world assets. These applications could give investors more ways to hold and use digital wealth without constantly trading volatile tokens.

Yet, security, reliable applications, and responsible financial products must develop alongside network capacity.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Ethereum’s market performance presents a contrasting picture. ETH is trading just a notch above $1,800. This leaves the coin 63% below its all-time high of $4,946. The decline highlights the gap between Ethereum’s technological ambitions and its current market valuation.

Ethereum’s network utility and ETH’s investment performance are also not interchangeable. More applications and transactions can strengthen the ecosystem, but they do not create proportional demand for ETH.

The token still plays an important role as Ethereum’s native transaction currency, staking asset, and collateral across decentralized finance. For this reason, continued growth in staking, stablecoins, and tokenized assets could strengthen ETH’s underlying investment narrative.

Buterin’s comments are bigger than a debate about housing affordability. He is effectively challenging the crypto industry to build assets and platforms that encourage long-term ownership rather than constant speculation.

Ethereum has several pieces of that foundation already, including proof-of-stake security, smart contracts, and an expanding financial ecosystem.

Its upcoming upgrades aim to improve the infrastructure supporting those applications. But the network still needs to prove that its technology can deliver dependable financial products at scale.

#5228. Revolut’s Italian Business Faces Court Oversight: 265 Warnings, Zero Suspicious Reports

All reviews, research, news and assessments of any kind on The Tokenist are compiled using a strict editorial review process by our editorial team. Neither our writers nor our editors receive direct compensation of any kind to publish information on tokenist.com. Our company, Tokenist Media LLC, is community supported and may receive a small commission when you purchase products or services through links on our website. A Milan court has put Revolut’s Italian branch under judicial administration for one year, in a ruling dated November 12 that came to light on Monday. The Revolut investigation found that the bank’s anti-money laundering checks let suspected criminals move money through it for five years.

Italy: A Milan court has placed the Italian operations of digital banking giant Revolut under judicial administration for one year after investigators uncovered serious anti-money-laundering failures involving mafia-linked suspects and convicted criminals.Prosecutors identified… pic.twitter.com/8b5WkfDdad

The court found that at least 24 clients moved or hid about €41.9 million through Revolut accounts between 2021 and 2026. All of them are under investigation or already convicted, and some have suspected mafia ties. Two court-appointed administrators will now work alongside the bank’s managers on customer checks and transaction monitoring.

We lined up the figures from the ruling. Other banks filed 265 suspicious-transaction reports on those same 24 people, about 11 each. Revolut filed none.

Revolut is not under criminal investigation, and it says its services in Italy, where it has more than 5 million customers, will keep running normally. The case also reaches into crypto. It began with a 2024 police inspection of Revolut Digital Assets Europe, the unit that serves the app’s crypto users in Europe.

The order targets Revolut Bank UAB, the Lithuanian-licensed bank that runs the Italian branch. Milan prosecutor Paolo Storari asked for it after the Revolut investigation by the Guardia di Finanza, Italy’s financial police.

Judicial administration is a preventive measure, not a penalty. Italian courts have used it on fashion and logistics companies to fix weak controls without taking over the business. In the 39-page ruling, the court said Revolut’s failures were “embedded in a stable management model, repeatedly applied over time.” Prosecutors called the bank a “financial reservoir” for serious criminals.

Revolut said it takes its “regulatory obligations and anti-money laundering controls extremely seriously” and will cooperate fully.

Crypto Expert Report: Follow The Money – Which Presales Are Attracting Crypto Whales in 2026?

The ruling’s sharpest number is the gap in suspicious-transaction reports, the alerts banks must send to Italy’s financial intelligence unit (UIF) when money looks dirty. Rival banks flagged the same 24 people 265 times. Revolut, which held their accounts too, sent nothing. That gap sits at the center of the Revolut investigation.

The suspects are linked to money laundering, tax fraud, extortion, and drug cases, some with suspected mafia ties. Prosecutors say there is no evidence that Revolut knowingly took part in their schemes. The case is about controls that didn’t catch them.

The Revolut investigation started with crypto. In 2024, Milan’s financial police inspected Revolut Digital Assets Europe, formerly RT Digital Securities Cyprus. That is the company that runs crypto trading for the app’s users across Europe, under a MiCA licence from Cyprus.

The police report, finished in December 2024, alleged more than 1 million breaches of customer due diligence and record-keeping rules and 60 failures to report suspicious transactions. It went to Italy’s Economy Ministry, which can fine the company. The ministry hasn’t opened sanction proceedings yet, and Revolut’s window to object runs into 2027.

Two more reviews are under way. The UIF has finished its own inspection of the Italian branch and is due to report soon. Bank of Italy inspectors are also checking how the bank handles transparency and customer-protection rules.

The Milan order adds to a run of trouble in Europe. Lithuania’s central bank fined Revolut Bank €3.5 million in April 2025 over gaps in how it monitored transactions, its largest fine at the time. In April 2026, Italy’s competition authority fined Revolut over €11 million for unfair practices, including blocking payment accounts without warning. Revolut said it would appeal.

The timing matters beyond Italy. Revolut has conditional approval for a US national bank charter. Cetin Duransoy, head of its US unit, said on Monday that “a massive hiccup somewhere” can have an impact in other places.

Counting from the November 12 ruling, the dates to watch are:

For Revolut’s customers in Italy, nothing changes today. Accounts, cards and crypto trading keep working, and the administrators don’t touch customer money. The risk is to the bank’s growth: stricter checks can mean more questions at sign-up and more frozen transfers, the same practice Italy’s watchdog fined it for in April.

#5227. Five Forged Receipts Drained $304.5K From Ankr's Ethereum Bridge Using a 0.0044 ankrETH Deposit

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

SlowMist says five forged receipts with valid signatures let an attacker drain about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum bridge using one old Optimism deposit. Here is how the check failed.Every one of the five receipts was signed by the bridge's own trusted signer. Every one pointed to a deposit that had already been paid out.

On November 9, an attacker drained about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge. According to SlowMist's alert, the attacker built five forged receipts that all referenced a single legitimate Optimism transaction, changing the recipient, the token and the withdrawal amount in each one.

All five carried valid signatures from the bridge's trusted consensus signer.

The reused transaction was tiny: a deposit of about 0.0044 ankrETH made on Optimism on November 3, which SlowMist's analysis says had already been redeemed on Ethereum the same day. Six days later, that one settled deposit was cited five times. The incident is recorded in the SlowMist Hacked database.Blockaid flagged the exploit as it unfolded, at about 08:42 UTC, with roughly $292,000 already gone. SlowMist followed at 09:14 UTC with the higher $304,500 estimate and an explanation of the forged receipts. Ankr paused withdrawals, and no recovery plan has been confirmed.

The design is common across lock-and-release bridges. A user deposits on the source chain, and an off-chain set of signers watches for that deposit and signs a receipt describing it. The destination contract, in this case Ankr's Ethereum bridge contract, checks that the receipt carries a valid signature and then releases the funds.That setup makes the signers the source of truth. The contract can't see Optimism, so it leans on the signature to prove the deposit happened. The weak point sits in the gap between "the signer signed this" and "this really happened." A contract that treats the first as proof of the second inherits every mistake the signing process makes.

SlowMist's finding is precise: the withdrawal function released assets without independently verifying the actual event on the source chain. A signature confirmed that the signer approved a message. It did not confirm that the message matched a deposit that existed, that was still unused, and that involved the same recipient, token and amount.The replay angle deserves attention, even though SlowMist's summary only implies it. A bridge normally marks each source event as consumed, keyed to something fixed like the source chain, transaction hash and log index, so it can be paid out once. If replay protection keys on the contents of the receipt instead, changing the recipient, token or amount produces a receipt the contract has never seen. Five edited receipts against one deposit would then look like five fresh claims. That is one plausible way the pieces fit together, not a finding the researchers have published.Bridge history offers parallels. In 2022, Wormhole lost about $325 million when an attacker got a forged message past its signature verification, and Nomad lost about $190 million after a misconfiguration let nearly any message pass as valid. The Ankr case is smaller, but it shares the same root: the verification step accepted something it shouldn't have.

The Ethereum transactions show the attacker extracted about 82.91 ankrETH, 515,206 ankrPOL and 7.98 million ANKR tokens. Blockaid described the five withdraw calls as using the tiny Optimism deposit to unlock the bridge's locked inventory and send it to a new wallet.The mix of assets tells its own story. Each forged receipt named a different token and amount, which suggests the attacker picked targets based on what the bridge held. That fits receipts built entirely by the attacker, apart from the one real transaction reference. Anyone wanting to trace them can open the bridge contract's transaction list on Etherscan and filter for the five `withdraw` calls on November 9.

The most important fact is still missing. SlowMist says the origin of the unauthorized signatures is under investigation, and it hasn't confirmed whether the signers were compromised.A valid signature on a forged receipt has a short list of explanations. A signing key, or the service holding it, could have been accessed. A signing service could have been tricked into signing attacker-supplied data. Or the signing logic itself could have a flaw that produces signatures for receipts it shouldn't. Each one points to a different fix: a stolen key means rotating signers, a manipulated service means tightening input validation off-chain, and a logic flaw means rewriting the signing rules.Whichever it turns out to be, the on-chain contract and the off-chain signer both failed to ask the same question. Either one verifying the source event would likely have stopped the attack, and neither did.

The lessons are narrow and practical. Replay protection should key on the immutable identity of the source event, not on the receipt's contents, and a source event should be consumable exactly once. The destination contract should confirm that the receipt's recipient, token and amount match what the source-chain event actually recorded, using a proof or an independent verifier instead of trusting the signer alone.Signer infrastructure needs its own scrutiny. Threshold schemes, hardware-backed keys and strict limits on what a signing service will sign all shrink the damage from a single failure. Rate limits and per-withdrawal caps help as well. A bridge that can release its entire locked inventory in five calls has no brake once a signature check is defeated.Trust in a bridge comes in layers, and one layer rarely holds up alone. Users with funds in Ankr's bridge should watch for the project's post-mortem and its plan for restoring withdrawals. For developers, the question to put to their own code is a blunt one: if a signer signs something false, what stops the contract from believing it?

#5224. PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery

David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI), used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing.

“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”

The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.

The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them. “It’s a negative result that allows people to know, okay, we’re no longer looking there,” Turturean said.

More broadly, it reflects the upheaval in the scientific world caused by AI problem-solving.

“A proof of full [Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture] was one of the last remaining open problems in quantum query complexity that everyone seemed to agree was centrally important,” Aaronson, who described himself feeling satisfied, awestruck, disappointed, and fatigued by the news, wrote. “I was surprised, honestly, to see it missing from OpenAI’s Mathocalypse dump a few weeks ago. Surely they tried it, so was it really so much harder than all the problems that were solved?”

That’s a point in favor of PSI’s model, which is to solve scientific problems with specialized model harnesses and scaffolding.

“An effective kind of research system should have lots of things related to harnesses, lots related to tools, memory systems, simulation infrastructure,” PSI CEO Matt Pines told TechCrunch. “You want to be able to really go after a problem at breadth and depth, and be able to consider a wide range of potential alternatives.”

For now, the company’s revenue comes from using its tools to optimize data centers, simulating the variables of heat, power, water, sound — “where the performance of that site as well as its impact on the community are a direct function of its physics.” The long play, however, is converting theoretical physics breakthroughs into actual technologies.

“Six to nine months ago, when I was talking to investors, like I had to sort of stretch to validate that conditional, right? Like, ‘no, no, no, trust me, pretty soon, theoretical physics is going to be mostly the domain of machines,’” Pines said. “And it’s not there yet, but it’s on its way.”

Still, while AI has claimed important solutions in fields like mathematics and computer science where it’s possible to express them in validated code, doing so in less abstracted disciplines like the life sciences or physics has proven more difficult. Last week, the startup Discovered Materials released a $1 million grand challenge for researchers using AI to understand problems like superconductivity and heat dissipation.

“At the end of the day, physics is different than math because it’s the real world … nature gets a vote in your models of reality,” Pines said. He said the startup is focused on understanding how to take computational results and validate them with experiments in the most efficient way possible.

“If it’s a true fact of nature, that’s a trick that you can exploit,” Pines said. “You could build a device out of it, right? The AI suggests an idea; it allows you to do something in the world you weren’t able to do before … and so each of those are kind of loops that PSI is building.”

As “neolabs for science” become a pathway for potentially groundbreaking science, the participants are still figuring out what the standards are for this new world. Because PSI had to hold its result until Anthropic’s model was nearly ready for release, they were able to share it with relevant researchers to better understand it.

“As an academic, we wanted to play our role in doing things the right way,” Jim Halverson, a professor at Northeastern University who advises PSI, said. He’ll be attending a summit at MIT next week where leading physicists will try to hash out a response to the new pace of science. “Best practices are still emerging … We figured that transparency is a good way to go, and contacting experts is a good way to go.”

“We had some time to sit on it … and it was the first time that I actually took one of my AI-elicited solutions on print, and I read through it, and I was like, okay, how can I make this … be presented more naturally for a human?” Turturean, who said the academic community will expect him to be able to explain the result, told TechCrunch. “And I think it also made me realize, oh my God, the weight of what AI can do.”

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has posted an alarming warning about Bitcoin (BTC), suggesting that the world's largest cryptocurrency might never return to its previous all-time high.

In a recent post on X, Brandt shared a weekly Bitcoin chart showing what appears to be a massive head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern commonly associated with a bearish trend reversal.

The legendary trader's warning comes amid one of Bitcoin's worst sell-offs this year, with the cryptocurrency losing nearly half of its value since reaching its record high in October 2025.

Brandt's chart shows Bitcoin forming a left shoulder, a higher peak representing the head, and a lower right shoulder. The cryptocurrency is now testing the neckline of this potential bearish formation, located around the $60,000 to $65,000 region.

Is this a legit H&S top in Bitcoin? If it is I can build a technical narrative that the ATH is in, not to be surpassed at least in my lifetime https://t.co/yoBq2Gp9UK

A confirmed breakdown below the neckline could indicate that Bitcoin has entered a prolonged bearish trend.

However, Brandt has not declared the pattern complete. His warning remains conditional on whether the formation proves to be a legitimate head-and-shoulders top.

Bitcoin suffered another massive crash on Saturday, Nov. 14, extending the losses that had already shaken the cryptocurrency market earlier in the week. The flagship cryptocurrency plunged to approximately $62,830, with its weekly losses exceeding 16%.

The downturn accelerated on Nov. 13, when Bitcoin fell below the psychologically important $70,000 level for the first time since August.

The selloff was initially triggered by worsening macroeconomic conditions, particularly stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data that increased expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December.

A stronger U.S. dollar and rising Treasury yields and the Nvidia chaos have also made riskier assets, including cryptocurrencies, less attractive to investors.

On Nov. 10, 2021, Bitcoin reached what was then a historic high of approximately $69,000.

Five years later, the cryptocurrency has fallen below that level.

For comparison, Bitcoin closed at approximately $65,467 on Nov. 14, 2021. At the $62,830 level shown on Brandt's chart, Bitcoin was trading roughly 4% below its price exactly five years earlier.

Bitcoin's most recent all-time high was recorded on Oct. 6, 2025, when the cryptocurrency surged above $126,000.

That historic rally was supported by strong institutional demand, substantial inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, and the increasingly crypto-friendly regulatory scene.

#5222. OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder

OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.”

However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners. Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent, it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses.

OpenAI’s spokesperson didn’t have more to share on its plans for travel-related products, except to say that travel is one of the areas that chatbot users frequently ask about. “1.2 billion people turn to ChatGPT each week for help with everyday tasks — from understanding their health, figuring out what to make for dinner, building a budget, and even planning a trip. We see a real opportunity to make these experiences even more useful,” the spokesperson said.

Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025.

When a key partnership with Marriott fell through, the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with over $600 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values.

So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store with travel now that he’s joined the company.

Note: This story was updated with OpenAI’s comments and updated revenue for Sonder.

#5221. Tom Lee Reveals Three Possible Reasons Behind Crypto Market Crash

Prominent market analyst and BitMine Immersion Technologies chairman Tom Lee has offered three potential explanations for the recent crypto market crash that has erased billions in market capitalization over the last few days.

Firstly, Lee points out that the recent crash in AI and semiconductor stocks, especially Nvidia, may have led to margin calls, particularly for retail investors in Asian markets.

According to the analyst, this scenario might have forced investors who needed more liquidity to cover their leveraged positions to sell other assets, including crypto.

Secondly, Lee explains that investors may be selling off their existing equity and crypto holdings to free up funds ahead of Anthropic’s upcoming IPO.

Lastly, the aftermath of the huge $6.3 billion Binance hack that occurred in late October may also be playing a role.

According to Lee, some account holders may be cashing out or converting their recovered funds into stablecoins, further contributing to the sell-off.

Aside from that, Lee has also cited potential risks posed by AI to existing cybersecurity systems and increased U.S. scrutiny of semiconductor sales to Asian markets, including China, as additional factors.

However, these are all just potential explanations rather than confirmed reasons for the downturn.

On Friday, Nov. 13, the world’s largest crypto asset, Bitcoin, fell below the psychological level of $70,000.

Further selling occurred on Saturday as BTC dropped below $66,000 and continued to decline to around $62,112 as of Sunday, its lowest level since July.

As for Ethereum, the losses are even worse, with ETH dropping to around $1,711, its lowest price since early July.

Major crypto assets like XRP and Solana (SOL) are also experiencing massive losses.

With such a sharp decline, there’s been another round of liquidations in the crypto market.

According to CoinGlass data, about $2 billion in leveraged crypto positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours, with the majority involving bullish traders.

Additionally, this crypto crash has coincided with massive outflows from crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

From Oct. 30 to Nov. 13, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw nearly $3 billion in net outflows, indicating that institutional investors are also selling off.

#5220. With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips

Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.

Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.

However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.

As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.

Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.

This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.

In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

The highly anticipated Anthropic IPO is set to test investor appetite for frontier AI companies amid explosive growth and heightened market caution. We look at how high ANT could go in 2026 and into 2027.

Will the ANT stock launch spark a fresh wave of bullish sentiment across the AI sector, or could it mark the top, triggering a death spiral as pressure builds on these tech companies?

Anthropic just dropped the IPO numbers:• 825M shares• $70–$78 range• Up to $64B raise• Ticker: $ANTPricing next week. Possible debut around Nov 19–20.Big one incoming. https://t.co/orSq5RbwKh

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models, is expected to price its initial public offering on November 18, 2026, with shares beginning to trade on the Nasdaq the following day under the ticker ANT.

The company is offering 825M Class A shares in a range of $70 to $78 each. At the top of the range, the public offering would raise approximately $64.35Bn.

In addition, Anthropic has arranged a concurrent $26Bn private placement of non-voting Class N shares with strategic partners including Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC.

Combined, the deals could bring in more than $90 billion in total proceeds. The offering implies a valuation of roughly $1.0–1.02 trillion on shares outstanding after the deal, or up to about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

I think what happens this week is that markets will be an illiquid shit show ahead of the Anthropic IPO, but the IPO will likely go forward anyways because the company needs the $100 billion. Analyst views span a wide range. Morningstar has assigned a fair-value estimate of $92 per share (implying roughly $1.7 trillion in equity value) and describes the IPO range as undervalued, with a bull-case target of $188.

Other independent models produce base-case valuations near or slightly above the IPO range and more optimistic scenarios well above $100 per share if enterprise adoption and revenue growth remain strong.

Skeptics point to the company’s enormous compute commitments (nearly $900Bn) and intense competition as reasons to be more cautious.

Talking about acceleration: In 13 months, the best AI agent went from completing 2.5% of real freelance projects on the Remote Labor Index to 41.3% with Claude Fable 5.2.These were paid projects that took human professionals 29 hours on average, with briefs provided and client… pic.twitter.com/FOy6wU4QWv

Anthropic IPO enters the public markets with exceptional momentum. Its annualized revenue run-rate reached approximately $81 billion by the end of October 2026, reflecting explosive growth from enterprise customers.

In early November, the company released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, its most capable models yet for coding, finance, scientific work, and security research.

Enterprise traction continues to deepen, with thousands of customers now spending six or seven figures annually. The company’s Public Benefit Corporation structure and emphasis on AI safety set it apart from purely commercial rivals.

Post-IPO catalysts that could drive a rally include further model advances, expansion of high-margin enterprise products, evidence that the heavy compute investments are translating into durable competitive advantages, and any broader recovery in AI-related stocks.

Assuming the IPO prices near the upper end of the $70–$78 range and the company continues its rapid revenue expansion while managing costs, shares could trade in a range of $110–$150 by the end of 2027 in a constructive environment.

This would reflect continued strong enterprise adoption, successful deployment of new model capabilities, and a more stable macro backdrop for high-growth technology names.

Upside beyond that range remains possible if Anthropic cements a clear leadership position in enterprise AI or if the broader AI investment cycle reaccelerates sharply. Conversely, intensified competition, slower-than-expected monetization, or renewed risk-off sentiment in tech could keep the stock closer to its IPO range or below.

Overall, the Anthropic IPO marks a major milestone for the AI sector, and Anthropic’s execution in the first 12–18 months as a public company will be decisive for its longer-term valuation trajectory.

Shiba Inu's value on exchanges is falling too rapidly and might hit levels below $300 million for the first time in the last 4 years. According to CryptoQuant, SHIB held on exchanges is now worth $331.96 million, down 6.81% in a day.

The bearish market is somewhat aggravating, and outflows from exchanges would certainly push the total value below this key threshold.

The key here is the rapidly decreasing market value rather than fund outflows. In tokens, the reserves went down by only 0.05%, with around 86 trillion SHIB still sitting on exchanges.

$332 million is somewhat of a baseline for Shiba Inu, essentially the whole supply available for sale. If someone triggers a full 86 trillion SHIB sellout, that batch will not be worth $332 million; we would be lucky to see one-third of it.

SHIB's liquidity is thin when measured against institutional appetite, as most holders are regular retail investors.

On the contrary, if Shiba Inu somehow recovers, an increase in fund injections is more than a possibility. For now, the netflow stays negative, with around 45.9 billion SHIB leaving exchanges over the last 24 hours.

Those flows most likely reflect usual trading activity, with investors constantly moving funds into self-custody or selling.

The price of the asset is doing no better: it invalidated the $0.000004 level and now bounces, even though the bounce is not followed by any surge in volume or momentum. It is purely caused by the oversold state of SHIB rather than anything else.

SHIB does not show a strong correlation with Bitcoin here, but rather with altcoins of the same echelon, most of which are oversold too.

SHIB dropped to around $0.0000037 on November 14, losing its July low of $0.00000413 along the way. RSI dipped below 30 at the same time, entering the oversold zone.

For the reserves to fall below $300 million, SHIB would have to drop to around $0.0000035, roughly 11% below the current price of $0.00000394.

#5217. Nine Korean startups vie for a spot in Disrupt 2027’s Startup Battlefield 200 competition

TechCrunch’s yearly Startup Battlefield 200 competition sees hundreds of companies from across the world trying every year to get a chance to pitch in front of VCs and the international tech community at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference.

This week, nine early-stage South Korean startups pitched at DETO 2026, a technology conference in Seoul, to earn a spot in next year’s Startup Battlefield 200.

The startups work across the deep tech sector, including healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors, and AI. All nine startups are looking to enter the U.S. market as part of the broader international expansion plans.

Voinosis, which develops AI to detect changes in brain health through voice analysis, won the competition. The other eight startups are listed below in alphabetical order.

Voinosis is developing an AI tool that analyzes speech patterns such as pitch, pauses, rhythm, and response times to detect changes linked to brain health. Each voice check takes less than five minutes.

The company says its technology has been tested in Greek, Japanese, and English, and its product doesn’t require separate training for each language. In a clinical study involving 146 participants, the startup claims its tech achieved 88% accuracy in screening for potential cognitive issues.

Voinosis targets hospitals, senior living facilities, insurers, and individual consumers. It also plans to link voice checks with cognitive training, assessments, and treatment provided by healthcare professionals.

The startup was founded by Grace Shin, who spent more than 25 years as an otologic surgeon. The startup is currently raising a Series A round and has already secured a South Korean pharmaceutical company as a strategic investor.

Awesome Lab, based in Seoul, makes ThermoFlux, a heating system that uses water electrolysis and ionization to generate heat. The system can manage heat production for buildings, water supply, and industrial processes. The company says its technology can reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions.

For its international expansion, Awesome Lab is taking a different approach in each market. In the U.S., it plans to supply core OEM modules and work with boiler, water heater, and HVAC companies on product development.

Crosshub helps travelers and international visitors verify their identities and set up payment methods abroad. Its platform, IDBlock, combines identity verification and payment services using self-sovereign identity (SSI) and zero-knowledge proof.

The company says its platform helps users prove their identity across borders without sharing unnecessary personal information. Crosshub is also integrating this technology with payment systems to improve access to financial services for travelers.

DeepFusion AI has developed a 4D radar-based imaging system with additional sensors for autonomous mobility, robotaxi, maritime surveillance, and defense applications. The system combines RF sensors with radar and lidar to detect objects, movement, or distance without a direct line of sight. All sensors are supposedly packed into a single, customizable unit.

EFLOW develops special motors that can produce more torque, or rotational force, while taking up less space for use in robots, drones, satellites, and other mobility applications. The startup also develops actuators that control how robotic joints move.

Otiton Medical makes two medical devices: One specializes in measuring body temperature, while another can capture ear canal images and analyze the eardrum. The company says its AI was trained on about 55,000 images of eardrums, and the device has received medical certification in South Korea.

Riibotics says it can deploy robots into warehouses within a day. Riibotics wants to reduce deployment costs for warehouses by streamlining setup, which includes infrastructure setup, warehouse mapping, system integration through custom middleware, task programming, and safety checks.

Ternell, a semiconductor startup based in Ulsan, is developing a new type of memory to help AI chips use less power.

Unlike conventional two-state memory, Ternell’s T-SRAM system adds a third state for more efficient data storage. Founded in 2019 by KyungRok Kim, a former Samsung Electronics engineer, Ternell reports that tests with 28-nanometer chips showed a 33% to 102% increase in memory capacity per area, and a 55% to 71% reduction in energy needed to access data, compared with conventional SRAM.

Testbank is a Korean edtech startup developing Solve, an app that converts printed study materials, such as workbooks and test-prep books, into interactive digital versions.

The startup uses AI to identify question and answer spaces in publishers’ PDF files while preserving the original layout. Solve lets you write answers directly on the page and be graded automatically.

#5216. Coinbase Brings ChatGPT Into Crypto Trading as Pancake Rebrand Signals Binance Rivalry

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Coinbase is bringing crypto trading directly into ChatGPT as competition for AI-powered financial services intensifies. Meanwhile, PancakeSwap has dropped “Swap” from its name, expanding beyond decentralized trading. The two developments show how Coinbase and Binance-linked crypto projects are positioning themselves for the next phase of digital finance.

Coinbase announced its ChatGPT integration last night, allowing users to connect accounts and manage portfolios. Users can check balances, analyze holdings, and place eligible trades using everyday language. And every order requires explicit approval before execution.

The timing coincides with Pancake’s attempt to reposition itself beyond its original decentralized exchange business.

Trade Base assets from ChatGPT@ChatGPT now connects to your Coinbase account, so you can trade Base assets in chat pic.twitter.com/tg9r2Iv3Qe

The Coinbase plugin allows eligible users to trade crypto and equities without leaving ChatGPT. Users can request market or limit orders through conversational instructions.

Before execution, ChatGPT displays an interactive confirmation card showing order details. Users must approve the transaction before Coinbase processes it through its Advanced Trade platform. Standard trading fees, eligibility requirements, and account limits still apply.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described the integration as another step toward an emerging agentic economy. The idea involves AI assistants handling increasingly complex financial tasks for users. But Coinbase still keeps humans responsible for approving individual trades for now.

To decentralize AI and preserve freedom, we need a coordination layer: a market economy where agents communicate and cooperate through prices.Teams of specialized open-weight models can outperform frontier models, just as a team of skilled people can outperform any single…

The integration also builds on Coinbase’s AI infrastructure. Its Coinbase for Agents toolkit provides developers with connections to trading accounts and market data. The ChatGPT launch brings those capabilities into a more accessible consumer interface.

As of today, the official integration currently remains limited to eligible U.S. Coinbase users. It also depends on ChatGPT account and workspace availability.

new brand, who dis?PancakeSwap is now Pancake 🥞6 years ago we were known for one thing. Today, we’re More Than a Swap. Let us reintroduce ourselves 👇 pic.twitter.com/J3P7Mocu2P

While Coinbase expands through ChatGPT, Pancake is changing how users perceive its decentralized trading ecosystem. Formerly known as PancakeSwap, the platform announced its rebrand today. The new identity reflects six years of expansion beyond its original token-swapping business.

Pancake now operates across more than 11 blockchain networks. The platform reports over 208 million users and more than $4.4 trillion in cumulative trading volume.

Its services now include perpetual contracts, tokenized stocks, ETFs, yield products, and developer infrastructure. The project is also preparing a dedicated mobile application. Its CAKE ticker and contract address remain unchanged, with existing staking positions unaffected.

Pancake’s relationship with Binance makes this rebrand interesting. Binance Labs announced a strategic investment in CAKE in June 2022. The investment supported the decentralized exchange’s development within the BNB Chain ecosystem.

The rivalry becomes clearer when looking beyond the latest announcements. Binance has already introduced its own AI infrastructure through Binance Agent OS. Launched in August 2026, the platform connects compatible AI applications with Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

Its Model Context Protocol server supports compatible AI agents, including ChatGPT. Developers can build applications that access supported Binance services through user-controlled permissions.

Pancake is also developing its position in this emerging market. In July, the platform partnered with BNB Chain’s Agent Studio to help developers deploy autonomous agents.

These agents can interact with Pancake’s liquidity pools, rebalance positions, and execute trading strategies. Its AI tools also include portfolio planning and assistance across DeFi products.

This creates an interesting contrast between the two ecosystems. Coinbase is bringing AI-powered trading directly to consumers through ChatGPT. Binance is building infrastructure that allows developers and AI agents to interact with its services. Pancake adds a decentralized execution layer to the wider BNB Chain ecosystem.

The next battle in crypto may not be about which exchange attracts the most human traders. It could be about which infrastructure becomes the preferred destination for AI-powered financial activity.

#5215. Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

The duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

“Phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” Zhang told TechCrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene.”

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Users can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

“For Phota, we built our own tech,” Zhang said. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo.”

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

The startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

“We have this obsession with authenticity,” Xia said. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’.”

Xia said beta users were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than AI-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

“We’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” Zhang said. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. So, I think that meant so much to us. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember.”

In terms of funding, the company raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

Phota Labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also plans to launch an Android app in the future.

#5214. New Monero Privacy Update Might Be Coming Soon: Key Improvement

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.

PR 11743 was opened on November 13 and is currently pending review. It is an updated version of a PR opened on November 8 by contributor vtnerd. After receiving feedback from another Monero developer, vtnerd, the PR was updated.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P and then passes it to the regular Monero network.

Currently, when a Monero node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P, it relays that transaction to the rest of the Monero network.

While the transaction is technically private as it travels into the node, once it reaches Monero's public peers, the transaction is no longer private. This PR proposes that Monero nodes will only accept transactions from Tor and I2P peers over incoming connections. Transactions received over outgoing Tor and I2P connections would be ignored.

Once accepted, the transaction would be subject to a random delay before being relayed to the rest of the Monero network using Monero's existing transaction relay protocol, Dandelion++. Currently, a user can instruct their node to broadcast their transaction immediately.

Over Tor and I2P connections, this request would be ignored. No transaction would be exempt from the random delay.Being able to link a transaction's timing between the anonymity network and the Monero network is an easy way to deanonymize a user. If a transaction is broadcast to the Monero network immediately after being received from Tor, an observer watching both networks can link the two.

This is a similar concept to a previous PR from vtnerd that would have introduced a randomized delay when relaying transactions from Tor and I2P to the Monero network.

While the amount of code that would need to be modified is not particularly large, this does close a hole for users that rely on Tor and I2P to obscure their location.

When the patch lands in a release is yet to be confirmed. The PR is also labeled for a backport, so it might reach the current release branch as well.

#5213. Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands

Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.

Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.

Announced Thursday, its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.

Nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.

Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.

Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.

Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.

“Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”

Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.

Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.

The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.

This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

#5211. How Bittensor's Gamma Turns Every AI Payment Into an Alpha Burn

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Paying a Bittensor subnet with gamma burns its alpha token. Here is how gamma gets minted, how the lower-price rule works and why the credit can never be converted back.Pay a Bittensor subnet for an AI answer with gamma, and your payment vanishes. The alpha token behind it gets burned, the credit gets spent, and nobody can redeem either one.

Using a subnet's service today usually means creating an account, adding funds and collecting an API key, and every additional subnet repeats the routine. Opentensor announced gamma to cut that friction. With gamma, a Bittensor wallet handles both access and payment across any subnet that adopts the standard.The mechanics are laid out in the gamma guide in the subtensor docs. Gamma is a credit a subnet can accept as payment, valued in US dollars. A customer gets it by burning that subnet's alpha token, and each dollar of burned alpha value mints one gamma, so a burn valued at $100 creates 100 gamma.Each balance stays tied to the subnet where it was created. Gamma minted for subnet 51 can't pay for a service on any other subnet. Root switches the system on network-wide, and each subnet owner or lease beneficiary then enables it for their own subnet.

Customers have two ways in. They can pay with TAO, and the protocol buys the subnet’s alpha and burns it in a single transaction. Or they can pay with alpha they already hold on that subnet, and the protocol burns it directly to create gamma.

Setup takes four steps. The customer creates a fresh hotkey that will act as an API key, associates it with their coldkey, looks up the service they want and mints. The docs give the command: btcli gamma mint --netuid 51 --hotkey API_KEY --amount-tao 10 --service-hotkey SERVICE_HOTKEY. The TAO route follows the same pool and flow accounting as stake-burn and creates no stake position. Users who hold stake can burn it with mint-gamma-with-stake, and --amount-alpha all burns the whole position.

The gamma lands in a deposit. Each deposit belongs to the minting coldkey and is keyed by the API-key hotkey, which signs the customer's requests. A hotkey holds at most one deposit per subnet, and a coldkey holds at most 64 per subnet. The docs warn against reusing a staking hotkey or a coldkey, because requests signed with the key get paid from the deposit.A few guardrails apply. A mint must reach at least 0.1 gamma. By default, the SDK quotes the mint first and fails it if the result lands more than 5% below the quote. The mint also needs a TAO/USD price no older than 300 blocks, about an hour.

Gamma’s valuation rule decides how much credit a burn buys. The protocol values the burned alpha in TAO, then converts that figure to dollars through an on-chain TAO/USD price feed. The TAO value equals alpha multiplied by the lower of two prices, the gamma price and the spot price, which the docs write as alpha × min(gamma price, spot price).

Every subnet keeps a gamma price. When a subnet registers, the price starts at the median alpha price across subnets. After that it moves asymmetrically. If spot falls, the gamma price falls to match at once. If spot rises, the gamma price climbs slowly toward it, closing a small slice of the gap each block, so the gap halves every 600 blocks, roughly two hours. However high spot jumps, the gamma price can at most double every 600 blocks.An example shows the effect. Say a user burns 100 alpha when spot sits at 0.05 TAO but the gamma price lags at 0.04. The mint uses 0.04, which gives 4 TAO of value, and at $400 per TAO that mints 1,600 gamma. Had the gamma price caught up, the same burn would mint 2,000, so the lag costs the burner 400 gamma. A short-lived pump buys no extra credit. The figures are illustrative, but the rule comes straight from the docs.The TAO/USD feed gets similar damping. A root-controlled oracle supplies the price, and the accepted price falls to a lower feed immediately but rises at most 66 parts per million per block, about 2% an hour. The docs admit the oracle is trusted: its accepted price can climb up to roughly 61% a day until root replaces or removes it.One more detail matters. The docs say alpha is valued at these prices, not at what selling it would return, so a burn that is large relative to the pool is worth more than a sale would be. A big burner gets credit for full value instead of a slipped sale price.Once minted, gamma holds its dollar value whether TAO or alpha prices rise or fall. Service providers still set their own prices.

To use a service, a person or an AI agent signs a request with a hotkey from their Bittensor wallet. The subnet owner, or another authorized account, deducts the required credits from that hotkey's gamma balance before delivering the service. Nothing transfers to anyone. The designated spender calls `spend-gamma` with up to 512 entries per call, each naming a hotkey, an amount and a 32-byte reference, and the spent gamma is destroyed on the spot.The reference doubles as a receipt. By convention it holds the service's own ID for the request being paid, returned with the response, so the customer can match each spend to a specific request. The chain repeats the reference in its events and reads it nowhere else, so an entry sent twice spends twice.Customers keep control throughout. The minting coldkey can set a daily spend cap that refills linearly over 7,200 blocks, about a day, and a cap of zero pauses the deposit. The coldkey can also change the spender, keep separate deposits for different apps and agents, and top up an existing deposit without switching hotkeys. Because the coldkey can pause or redirect at any moment, services spend ahead: they spend what they are about to serve, then serve what was spent. A spender can hand this right to a `GammaSpend` proxy, which can make no other call.Both minting and spending leave public records on-chain, so anyone can audit how much credit a subnet has created and how much customers have used.

The limits are strict. Gamma can't be transferred to another wallet, and it can't be converted back into alpha or TAO. It confers no claim on any party and can't be redeemed. Each subnet chooses whether, and at what prices, it accepts its own gamma.

The docs flag the sharpest risk directly: dissolving or pruning a subnet destroys all of its gamma, and holders receive nothing. A customer who prepaid a large deposit to a subnet that later shuts down loses it. Moving gamma between your own deposits is allowed, and a deposit opened under someone else's hotkey stays yours, since you can pull the gamma back at any time.A coldkey swap adds a few wrinkles. While one is announced, the coldkey's gamma calls are refused, though its spenders keep spending. After a subnet owner swaps coldkeys, deposits that name the old one keep it until the owner republishes its service.

The docs answer the economic question in one sentence: spent gamma pays its spender nothing. The value of the burned alpha accrues to the subnet's alpha holders.

That makes gamma a direct demand mechanism for alpha. Creating gamma always burns the subnet's alpha, which removes those tokens from circulation for good. When customers pay with TAO, the protocol first buys alpha from the subnet's pool, so TAO-funded purchases add buying pressure before the burn. Every dollar of AI usage ties a purchase of service credits to a burn of alpha.

A service operator earns through the alpha it holds and the emissions its subnet receives, not through a payment from customers. The structure rewards subnets that attract real usage, since usage shrinks their alpha supply.Two questions remain open. Customers get dollar-denominated credit, but the burn that funds it follows alpha prices, so heavy usage during a price spike may feel expensive. Holders also carry the dissolution risk, which will push careful buyers toward established subnets. Which services accept gamma, and at what price, will show whether this becomes a real payments layer or a niche tool. The mechanism is clear, and adoption is the unknown.

#5210. AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation

Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday.

That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago, led by IVP.

LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence.

With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use.

True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well (case in point is newcomer Mintive). However, LangChain has had a head start and now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including big-name startups like Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) has printed a death cross for the first time in 14 months on its daily chart. The 50 MA is below the 200 MA. This death cross follows the last signal, which was back in September 2025.

The latest death cross signal coincides with a sharp price drop, with Shiba Inu falling to unusually low levels below $0.000004.

Cryptocurrencies tumbled over the weekend, with Shiba Inu dropping sharply to a low of $0.0000037 on Saturday, marking four straight days of declines since November 11.

A death cross was completed on its daily chart, reflecting the ongoing selling pressure in the market. Crypto has been pummeled in recent weeks by a confluence of factors; liquidations accelerated over the last 24 hours, reaching a total of $1.96 billion across the market, according to CoinGlass data.

Unlike the abrupt crashes that have punctuated previous crypto downturns, much of the preceding decline unfolded during relatively subdued trading before liquidations accelerated in recent days.

The latest selloff is testing the resolve of some of the cryptocurrency market’s most committed investors, as a succession of setbacks pushes prices toward their lowest levels of the year and major sources of demand weaken.

Stablecoin supply is shrinking fast, dropping $17 billion over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022. As holders swap stablecoins for fiat, they drain buying power from BTC and crypto, analysts at Glassnode said.

It remains to be seen whether buying power returns to the market. According to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a big buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when."

Shiba Inu rebounded from a low of $0.0000037 on Sunday, but the meme coin remains down 6.87% over the last 24 hours and down 14% over the week.

Further recovery will occur if dip buying gains traction, with the daily 50 MA and 200 MA at $0.000005 marking resistance levels for SHIB's price. Support is expected at $0.000003 if the declines continue.

#5208. Tokenized Stocks Open 24/7 on OKXICE, but Only Crypto Firms Signed Up: Will Wall Street Follow?

All reviews, research, news and assessments of any kind on The Tokenist are compiled using a strict editorial review process by our editorial team. Neither our writers nor our editors receive direct compensation of any kind to publish information on tokenist.com. Our company, Tokenist Media LLC, is community supported and may receive a small commission when you purchase products or services through links on our website. Click here for a full list of our partners and an in-depth explanation on how we get paid.

OKXICE, the joint venture of crypto exchange OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), opens round-the-clock trading in tokenized stocks for eligible US customers on Sunday, November 23. The only companies whose shares it will offer at launch are crypto firms: Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, BitGo and Securitize.

Of the 62 companies the venue first picked, 56 objected. Its November 5 notice lists 67 objectors in all, including every member of the Magnificent Seven.

⚡️JUST IN: OKX and NYSE parent ICE will launch 24/7 tokenized U.S. securities trading on November 23 through their joint venture, OKXICE.More than 70 assets are expected, including Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood, and Strategy securities, plus 59 Direxion ETFs.The platform will… pic.twitter.com/TfRuuZrcV0

That leaves buyers with a narrow menu. We checked what they will actually get: the six stocks are down a median 42% this year, while the S&P 500 is up 7%. Five of the six have moved more closely with Bitcoin than the S&P 500 has over the past three months.

The launch is the first real test of a new SEC rule meant to bring listed shares onto blockchains. So will Wall Street follow, or is this a crypto-only market for now?

Explore: Will Tokenized Stocks Move by xStocks Bring New Volume to HSBC, Shell and Other European Equities?

A tokenized stock is a blockchain token that tracks a listed share. ICE set up the venture after it invested in OKX in March at a $25 billion valuation. On OKXICE, each token is backed by a real US share, and customers hold it in a self-custody wallet inside the OKX app.

The venue runs under an exemption the SEC issued on September 17. It lets blockchain venues trade tokenized versions of listed US shares without registering as an exchange, for up to five years. Companies are not asked to opt in. Instead, each one gets 30 days after being notified to object, and silence counts as consent.

Most said no. Applied Optoelectronics said it was worried about pricing, liquidity and volatility, and that investors might think it backed the product. The OKXICE launch page confirms the November 23 start, with more than 70 assets, 59 of them exchange-traded funds from Direxion.

Crypto Expert Report: Follow The Money – Which Presales Are Attracting Crypto Whales in 2026?

We pulled daily prices for the six launch stocks from Yahoo Finance. Then we measured how far each has moved in 2026 and how closely its daily moves tracked Bitcoin over the past 90 trading days.

So a US investor who wanted Apple or Nvidia around the clock gets, for now, five stocks that rise and fall with the crypto market. ICE’s own shares, by comparison, are up 8% this year and barely track Bitcoin at all, with a correlation of 0.08.

The objections don’t mean Wall Street is ignoring tokenization. It is building its own version first.

In March, the SEC approved a Nasdaq pilot that puts tokenized and regular shares in the same order book. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which settles most US stock trades, runs a tokenization service with 20 participants and 34 securities. In September, Nasdaq agreed to invest $100 million in Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, to build infrastructure for tokenized shares.

The difference is control. In those projects, exchanges and clearing houses run the system, and trading stays tied to regular market hours and rules. OKXICE offers 24/7 trading, which companies have pushed back on: a share that trades all weekend leaves no quiet time to handle bad news. Nasdaq has also warned that splitting trading across separate venues could thin out liquidity.

So the answer is “not yet.” Wall Street is likely to reach tokenized stocks through its own exchanges and DTCC before it lets crypto venues list its shares.

Robinhood is the launch name with the most at stake: it already sells tokenized stocks to European customers. Its 24/7 contract on Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange that lists perpetual futures on US stocks, trades at $70.32.
