#5184. NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

New tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics said the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to update their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

#5183. Brazil Takes Aim at Stablecoins With Shocking Money Laundering Claim

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s important to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

On April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore company.

This company, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows users to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

In a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

#5182. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

Bitcoin is trading near $69,200 after another sharp daily decline. The chart shows that BTC has broken below the $75,000–$76,000 support zone, which now represents an important resistance area. The immediate level to watch is around $69,000.

A sustained break below it could expose the $64,000–$65,000 support area, followed by $60,000. On the upside, Bitcoin would need to reclaim $75,000 to signal a potential recovery and improve its short-term outlook.

Bitcoin faces several challenges heading into the next difficulty adjustment. The increase in miner-to-exchange transfers, combined with negative demand indicators, suggests that the market is struggling to attract sufficient buying interest.

Still, the Antpool transfers should not be interpreted as proof of widespread miner capitulation. The data identifies a large movement from one mining pool, but does not establish that the coins were sold.

The upcoming difficulty reduction could improve mining conditions and help struggling operators manage their costs. However, it is unlikely to resolve the broader weakness in Bitcoin demand.

Investors will be watching whether exchange transfers translate into actual selling and whether spot-market buyers return. A recovery in demand would help absorb additional supply and provide a stronger foundation for Bitcoin’s next move.

#5181. Vitalik Buterin Breaks Silence on New Ethereum (ETH) Update

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

With the update, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of new accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

Unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

Glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The new date is yet to be confirmed.

Vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

Setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

#5180. Major Wealth Advisor With $24 Billion in Assets Discloses XRP ETF Stake

Major U.S. wealth management company EP Wealth Advisors has revealed that it holds an investment in an XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF). This was disclosed in the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the company submitted to the commission on Nov. 13. The filing showed that the investment was valued at $147,936 at the end of the third quarter.

Furthermore, the filing showed that the total portfolio value reported by EP Wealth Advisors stood at $24,380,879,896. This value comprises 1,603 items in the company's 13F information table.

It's worth noting, however, that this isn't the company's total assets under management. It's the value of its reportable securities holdings. There are also assets that are not included in Form 13F.

Interestingly, this isn't the first time EP Wealth Advisors has held an investment in XRPI. Data from its historical 13F filings shows that in the second quarter of 2026, the wealth management company held 13,425 shares in XRPI.

The recent filing shows that the company has now increased the number of shares it holds in the XRP ETF by 4,975 shares. This represents about a 37% increase in the company's XRPI holdings during the third quarter.

Nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the company's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that shows institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

The Volatility Shares XRP ETF was launched in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is currently trading on Nasdaq.

XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

This ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

As of Nov. 13, the most recent available data from the fund issuer shows that XRPI's net assets stood at about $77.9 million.

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has replied to XRP holders who criticized him for selling most of his XRP with a Saturday Night Live GIF of Natalie Portman saying, "I never said I was a role model."

According to Schwartz, his XRP holdings are down 88%, from a peak of roughly 26 million tokens to 3 million. His Bitcoin went from about 1,500 coins to one, and his Ether went from about 40,000 to six.

Schwartz wrote that he "really doesn't like risk." According to Schwartz, he and his wife agreed years ago to sell some of their coins every time crypto reached a new all-time high. In 2025, Schwartz sold around 2.5 million XRP and paid about $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. He had received these tokens in 2020 and 2023.

@hllywd22 @tchdwntommyd @WHTBOYRICKY @CryptoTaxFixer When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous. What BTC hit $200, that seemed ridiculous.

Schwartz said that all of his sales were made under written trading plans, and a lawyer approved each plan at least 30 days before each sale. According to Schwartz, his largest risk asset is still his stake in Ripple.

Schwartz also said that he was a skeptic from the start and did not believe in the early price records of crypto. "When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous," he wrote.

In his view, the price of XRP today depends on overall sentiment in the crypto market, and fees on the network barely move it. Schwartz allows that the token could capture some of the value of a successful ecosystem in the future, but there are no guarantees. On Monday, the price of XRP stands at $0.956.

On Nov. 16, Schwartz also posted a review of the XRPL codebase by the Qwen AI model. "I asked Qwen to rate my work on the XRPL software. It was mostly good. But this was harsh and it's not wrong," he wrote.

According to the review, the overall architecture of XRPL is good. Still, Qwen said that some components of the code are too tightly coupled, and the migration to a new testing framework stopped halfway. The AI model also called the code generation in XRPL opaque.

Several XRPL developers replied to the post and said that they are already rewriting some of these parts of the code. Other users asked for formal verification of the XRPL core before the new features planned for 2027 go live.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 is bringing a few major updates, including an added NACS charge port on all plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models.

The RAV4 was Toyota’s best-selling nameplate in the US last year and consistently ranks among America’s most popular vehicles alongside the Ford F-Series and Chevrolet Silverado.

For the 2027 model year, Toyota added several notable upgrades. The 2027 Toyota RAV4 will be available with hybrid (HEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains, with available front- or all-wheel drive (AWD).

The biggest change is that all 2027 RAV4 PHEV models now have a built-in NACS charge port with Level 3 DC fast-charging capabilities.

The NACS port is on the driver’s side and lets drivers use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. All PHEV grades also include an 11 kW onboard AC charger.

Powered by Toyota’s sixth-generation PHEV system, the plug-in RAV4 has standard AWD with a combined output of 321 horsepower. The setup includes a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, two electric motors, and a high-capacity traction battery.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV offers up to 52 miles of pure electric range on the base SE trim. It will be available in four trims: SE, XSE, Woodland, and GR Sport.

Toyota updated the suspension system in the Woodland grade for the 2027 model year with new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, giving it 9.1″ of ground clearance.

The Woodland trim adds a rugged look with standard All-Terrain tires, Roof Rails with Cross Bars, and a Tow Hitch Receiver. It also features new all-weather floor and cargo mats.

Lastly, the RAV4 GR Sport trim is for those who want a more performance-oriented, sporty style, with GT-tuned suspension and steering, sports seating, and a standard PHEV powertrain with AWD.

Inside, the 2027 RAV4 includes a standard 12.3″ digital cluster and a 10.5″ touchscreen with the Toyota Audio Multimedia system, plus wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

A 12.9″ touchscreen with a JBL Premium Audio system with 9 speakers is standard on the Limited trim and available on the XSE grade.

All 2027 Toyota RAV4s come with standard Toyota Safety Sense 4.0, which includes safety and convenience features such as Lane Departure Alert with Steering Assist, Full-Speed Range Dynamic Radar Cruise Control, Proactive Driving Assist, and a Pre-Collision System with Pedestrian Detection.

#5175. Satoshi’s Bitcoin DNA in XRP Ledger Uncovered in Two Cryptographic Mechanisms

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

In 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

Vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

Vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

However, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days."

The second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve."

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

MacPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees."

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”

Toto Finance, a company led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near New Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, announced its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”

The AI bubble debate is getting harder to dismiss as the Federal Reserve highlights more than $3 trillion in potential financial commitments tied to the advanced-computing buildout. Peter Schiff believes the boom could end in a crisis worse than 2008. But the Fed’s findings reveal a more complicated risk beneath the technology rally.

In a November 17 warning, Peter Schiff compared the artificial intelligence boom with the subprime mortgage market, arguing that easy monetary conditions have helped inflate asset valuations. His prediction is severe, but the financing figures now emerging from the Federal Reserve give investors a reason to examine the risks more closely.

Housing market index: 25, lowest since 2012. Nasdaq: down 12.25%. CoreWeave: down 64%. Bitcoin: down 33.5% from its 2026 high. Still think this is just about AI?New Episode: https://t.co/DGp4OQqtu1https://t.co/DGp4OQqtu1

The Federal Reserve’s November 13 Financial Stability Report shows how quickly financing for advanced computing has expanded.

Debt issuance linked to advanced computing infrastructure exceeded $680 billion by October 2026, roughly five times the $130 billion recorded in 2023. It also represented around 31% of nonfinancial investment-grade corporate debt issuance in 2026, compared with less than 6% three years earlier.

Outstanding public debt connected to advanced computing exceeded $1.1 trillion.

Those figures do not prove an AI bubble is about to burst. They do show how much capital is flowing into the infrastructure supporting the technology boom.

The more striking figure involves obligations beyond conventional borrowing.

The Fed’s report describes more than $1 trillion in undiscounted values for leases that have not yet commenced. It also identifies more than $2 trillion in other obligations, including take-or-pay contracts and residual-value guarantees.

That distinction matters. These commitments should not be described as $3 trillion in outstanding loans or realized losses. They represent future financial obligations and guarantees that could become more difficult to manage if demand or expected returns disappoint.

Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr also discussed the potential scale of AI-related leases, contracts and guarantees in a November 16 speech, putting their maximum nominal value above $3 trillion.

Another concern is the growing financial connection between major technology companies and AI startups.

Large technology firms and chipmakers have invested heavily in AI labs and cloud-computing businesses. Some recipients then spend money on computing services or hardware supplied by those same investors.

That creates a complicated relationship between investment, customer demand and reported business growth. It does not automatically mean the revenue is artificial, but it raises questions about how sustainable demand would be if outside funding slowed.

The Fed also highlights guarantees tied to data-center equipment and computing infrastructure. If hardware depreciates quickly or demand falls short, the value supporting some financing arrangements could weaken.

Schiff’s warning deserves attention, but it should not be mistaken for a Federal Reserve forecast.

The Fed identifies vulnerabilities involving elevated valuations, complex financing and the possibility of a sharp correction in AI-related equities. Its report also notes that market contacts are concerned about circular financing and heavy reliance on debt.

However, the report does not declare that a crisis is inevitable. It also describes the broader financial system’s resilience, including capital and liquidity buffers at large banks.

For investors, the real question is whether future AI earnings can justify the enormous investment now being made in infrastructure.

A sharp reversal in AI valuations could extend beyond technology stocks. Companies, lenders and investors connected through financing arrangements could face pressure if expected returns weaken.

That could also affect other risk assets if investors reduce exposure, sell leveraged positions or become more cautious about growth investments. Crypto markets could feel that pressure through broader risk aversion and leveraged liquidations, although the Fed’s findings do not establish that an AI downturn would cause a specific Bitcoin price decline.

The AI bubble warning is worth taking seriously, but a crash is not a foregone conclusion. Investors should watch earnings, infrastructure spending, debt issuance and the ability of AI businesses to turn enormous capital commitments into sustainable cash flows. That’s a more useful test than simply betting on Peter Schiff’s prediction.

Some traders think giant IPOs pull money out of crypto as investors sell other assets to buy in. Here is what Bitcoin did before, during and after the SpaceX listing, and what that could mean for the Anthropic debut.

Solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was announced on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.

Solana launched on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status."

The Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

"For users, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

According to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

Firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation said.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

"A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once."

Earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

#5165. New Jersey is putting 10 MW of community solar on warehouse roofs

Warehouse roofs are prime real estate for solar, and Faropoint is putting more of that underused space to work in New Jersey. The industrial property owner has started construction on the first of 16 community solar projects totaling more than 10 megawatts (MW).

First up is a 1.6 MW rooftop array at 19-05 Nevins Road in Fair Lawn. Another 15 projects, totaling about 8.5 MW, have been accepted into New Jersey’s Community Solar Energy Program, and nine are already cleared to start construction.

That’s more solar going onto buildings that are already there, with participating households set to get savings on their electricity bills.

Large warehouse roofs offer something solar developers need: lots of flat space. Putting panels up there gives the same building the job of generating electricity without taking up additional land.

Faropoint specializes in industrial properties used for local deliveries and distribution. “Utilizing previously unused portions of our buildings allows us to support the communities where we invest,” said Brian Nave, Faropoint’s vice president of asset management and renewable energy.

Faropoint and its independent solar adviser, SolarKal, expect the 16 projects to generate around 12.7 million kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity annually once they’re operating. They estimate the portfolio will avoid about 8,500 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions a year.

Faropoint says at least half of each project’s capacity will be reserved for low- and moderate-income households. New Jersey’s program requires a minimum of 51%.

A US judge acquitted two brothers accused of causing $25 million in losses to Ethereum trading bots.

The Ultrasound relay released transaction data without checking two zeroed block-header fields.

Prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentation required for wire fraud.

The Ethereum MEV exploit case has ended in acquittal after a US federal judge cleared two brothers accused of causing approximately $25 million in losses to automated trading bots. The deciding detail? The relay released transaction data without checking two critical fields in a block header.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno on November 16, 2026, ruling that prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentation required for wire fraud. The decision closes the government’s first criminal prosecution centred on an Ethereum MEV exploit.

The alleged operation took place in April 2023. Prosecutors said the brothers used eight bait transactions to attract sandwich-trading bots, which profit by placing trades around other users’ orders.

When their validator received a proposed block through the Ultrasound relay, it signed a block header with two critical fields set to zero. Those values described a block that couldn’t be valid.

But the relay didn’t check them. It released the block’s transaction contents anyway, allowing the brothers to construct a different block and replace the bait transactions with trades that worked against the bots.

The operation caused approximately $25 million in bot losses in around 12 seconds.

🚨 BREAKING: U.S. JUDGE ACQUITS TWO BROTHERS IN $25 MILLION ETHEREUM EXPLOIT CASEA major legal development in the cryptocurrency industry.A U.S. federal judge has acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, two MIT-educated brothers accused of extracting approximately $25… pic.twitter.com/LYZipaQP1r

The judge found that prosecutors hadn’t shown the disputed fields influenced the relay’s decision. Without that connection, the alleged false information couldn’t establish the material misrepresentation required for the wire fraud case.

Clarke also rejected the argument that bait transactions promised bots a particular execution order. Ethereum‘s public mempool doesn’t guarantee that pending transactions will be included or executed in a specific sequence.

The brothers were indicted in May 2024. Their first trial ended in a mistrial in November 2025 after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict.

The November 16 acquittal covered wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

It doesn’t make every MEV strategy or exploit legal. But this Ethereum MEV exploit ruling draws a clear distinction between questionable trading conduct and the specific deception prosecutors must prove in a criminal fraud case.

The XRP rich list shows that smaller holders continued accumulating XRP even as the price dropped below $1. Wallets holding between 10,000 and 100,000 XRP added around 504 million coins over the past year as per XRPScan data.

The number of wallets holding at least 10,000 XRP reached 343,897 on November 14, 2026, up around 5% since February, based on Santiment data.

However, the total XRP held by these wallets remained almost unchanged at 65.5 billion. This suggests that some existing holders may have spread their coins across multiple wallets rather than making new purchases.

The growth in the XRP rich list is mainly coming from wallets holding between 10,000 and 100,000 XRP.

This group added nearly 25,000 accounts over the past year. Its total holdings also increased by around 504 million XRP. During the November price decline, these wallets added another 39 million XRP.

The trend is different among holders with 100,000 to 1 million XRP. Their wallet count declined slightly from 30,500 in November 2025 to 30,300 on November 14, 2026.

This indicates that smaller holders are adding XRP, while the mid-sized holder group has remained largely unchanged.

Between November 6 and November 12, around 440 million XRP moved into three new or nearly empty wallets.

None of the receiving wallets had an exchange label on XRPScan. However, their owners remain unknown.

The transfers could represent existing holders moving their coins, a custodian managing assets for clients or a fund reorganizing its holdings. Therefore, the movement does not confirm fresh buying.

Exchange and company wallets account for a large share of the XRP rich list.

According to analyst cheeky crypto, at least half of the XRP held in wallets containing 10,000 coins or more belongs to accounts labeled as exchanges, companies or known individuals. Exchanges and companies alone account for more than 40%.

The concentration is higher among the largest wallets holding at least 100 million XRP, where around 84% of the coins are linked to exchanges and insiders, including Upbit, Coinbase, Binance and Ripple.

By comparison, only around 5% of the holdings in the 100,000 to 1 million XRP category are linked to labeled entities.

This difference is important because exchange wallets can hold XRP for many customers. Their balances do not necessarily represent the investments of individual whales.

Between November 4 and November 15, labeled exchange and company wallets outside Ripple added approximately 18 million XRP to their combined holdings.

During the same period, Binance-labeled wallets decreased by around 126 million XRP, while Upbit and Coinbase each added approximately 50 million XRP.

The figures suggest that coins moved between exchanges rather than showing a major overall increase in exchange holdings.

Previous market declines show that XRP has recovered after periods of increasing wallet numbers, but the trend does not guarantee a price rise.

During the April 2025 sell-off, XRP gained around 30% within 30 days of reaching its low while the number of wallets holding at least 10,000 XRP continued to increase.

A similar pattern occurred in August 2026. XRP recovered approximately 29% in the month after reaching a low of around $0.99 on August 16.

However, the token later lost those gains and declined further.

In November 2024, XRP gained around 174% in a month even though the 10,000 XRP wallet count remained relatively flat.

These examples show that changes in wallet numbers alone cannot explain or predict XRP price movements.

For now, the XRP rich list points to continued accumulation among smaller holders, while mid-sized wallet activity remains flat. The 440 million XRP transfer into fresh wallets adds another development to watch, but it does not establish whether new investors are entering the market.

#5156. US and Canada Announce Massive Crypto Fraud Crackdown

Authorities in the United States and Canada have announced a major cross-border crackdown on cryptocurrency fraud, bringing together law enforcement agencies, financial regulators and private companies to target online scam networks.

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) announced on Nov. 16 the launch of Operation Niagara, a coordinated initiative aimed at disrupting organized cryptocurrency fraud schemes and protecting potential victims.

According to the Canadian securities regulator, the operation involves investigators, securities specialists and financial crime experts from both countries.

The initiative will use advanced technology and enhanced investigative capabilities to identify fraudulent activity and potential victims in near real time.

Importantly, the operation will not focus solely on investigating criminals after fraud has occurred. Authorities also intend to identify individuals who are being targeted by scammers and intervene before they suffer further financial losses.

"Fraud knows no border, and it targets everyday people," said Bonnie Lysyk, Executive Vice-President of Enforcement at the OSC.

The initiative brings together several major law enforcement and regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Secret Service, Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

Canadian securities regulators, including the Alberta Securities Commission, British Columbia Securities Commission and Autorité des marchés financiers, are also participating.

Private-sector companies will contribute technical expertise and intelligence to help authorities identify and disrupt fraudulent networks.

It’s worth noting that the OSC didn’t provide details on how many fraud networks it is targeting, how many potential victims have been identified or how much cryptocurrency is involved in Operation Niagara.

#5154. Musk Joins 160,000 Signers Calling for Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Comeback: How Is NVDA Stock Reacting?

Jensen Huang petition goes viral and Elon Musk joins 160,000 signers. Return odds doubled Sunday and Nvidia jumped 3%, then faded. Levels to watch.

Elon Musk said on Friday, November 13, that he is signing the Jensen Huang petition, an open letter asking Nvidia’s board to bring back its former chief executive. Huang resigned a day earlier, after reports of extramarital affairs.

By Monday, the “Stand with Jensen” letter had more than 160,000 signatures. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick have also backed it. The letter asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts.

SILICON VALLEY VS. WHITE HOUSE: BATTLE FOR NVIDIA

Tech executives are pushing to reinstate Jensen Huang, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly opposes his return.

A petition backing Huang has drawn 175,000 signatures.

Yet prediction markets give Huang just an 18%… pic.twitter.com/BZl5KheVnq

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 16, 2026

We matched Polymarket’s odds of Huang’s return with a 24/7 Nvidia stock contract on Hyperliquid. Musk’s post lifted the odds but barely moved the stock. A sharper jump in the odds on Sunday evening did: the stock rose 3% within two hours, then gave it all back by Monday.

So how is Nvidia’s stock reacting, one day before earnings?

Musk posted on X that “a petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.” He had said earlier that hiring Huang would be “an honor.”

The petition is hosted at standwithjensen.com. Signers report their own job titles, and the site does not verify them. More than 7,500 say they work at the company, about 18% of its staff.

The company says it is choosing a search firm for the CEO role and has not formally approached any candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress runs the company in the meantime.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

Nasdaq is shut on weekends, but the stock still trades around the clock as a perpetual contract, a futures-style contract with no expiry date, on Hyperliquid. To see whether the Jensen Huang petition moved the stock, we lined up its hourly price with Polymarket’s odds that Huang rejoins by December 31, 2026.

Polymarket’s longer bets show how far the Jensen Huang petition still has to go. Traders give Huang a 37.5% chance of rejoining by the end of 2027, but only 5.6% by November 30.

On the daily chart, Hyperliquid’s NVDA contract trades at $156.93. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $199.26, and its 200-day EMA at $206.42. On Nasdaq, the shares closed Friday at $162.85, down 18.6% since November 4.

The Jensen Huang petition has moved the odds more than the stock. Musk’s backing barely shifted the price, and Sunday’s jump faded within a day. Tuesday’s earnings, the first under Kress, are likely to matter more to Nvidia shares than any petition.

#5153. Segway launches new electric motorcycle that’s so safe it has seatbelts

Segway came to EICMA this year with a surprisingly broad lineup of new electric motorcycles, ranging from high-performance concepts to off-road machines. But perhaps the most interesting of the bunch is also the one that looks the least like a conventional motorcycle or scooter.

Meet the Segway X Cruiser, an electric two-wheeler that takes motorcycle safety so seriously that it has a roll cage and seatbelts.

Or at least, those are among the configurations Segway is showing as it develops the new machine for production.

The X Cruiser is Segway’s attempt to bring more automotive-style protection to a single-track vehicle, essentially asking how much of a car’s safety envelope can be wrapped around a motorcycle without adding another pair of wheels.

From the looks of things, the answer is quite a lot.

Segway says the X Cruiser’s design was informed by automotive crash scenarios, with cage and semi-cage structures, four-direction collision protection, staged energy absorption, and seatbelt restraints intended to improve rider protection. It also gets active safety features including standard blind spot detection and lane change warning.

The company showed several ways that basic idea can be configured, ranging from a more conventional partially enclosed scooter-like setup to versions with significantly more structure surrounding the rider. One of the most striking configurations uses a heavily bolstered race-car-style seat and seatbelt along with protective framing around the rider, while another adds a roof for even more enclosure.

It’s a fascinating approach because motorcycles have traditionally relied largely on the rider wearing the protection. Helmets, jackets, gloves, boots and sometimes airbag vests form the safety system, while the motorcycle itself generally offers little physical protection during a crash.

The X Cruiser effectively flips part of that equation by building some of the protective structure into the vehicle itself.

There’s an important caveat here, though. Segway specifically notes that its descriptions refer to the vehicle’s current design and equipment and do not mean it has completed automotive-style crash certification. Final equipment and certification will depend on individual markets, so it sounds like the company is holding short of making any major certification claims. Still though, it’s easy to see how having what is effectively a racing seat and roll cage surrounding the rider could seriously contribute to better protection in a crash. Just remember to keep your hands and feet within the vehicle at all times.

And unlike plenty of wild EICMA showpieces, this one isn’t merely destined to live under convention-center spotlights. Segway says the X Cruiser has a confirmed mass-production plan, with launches planned for China and Europe between 2027 and 2028. There’s no US availability announcement yet.

Underneath all that protective hardware is a fairly serious electric touring platform. Segway is using its CTB (cell-to-body) battery integration to help improve structural rigidity and battery packaging, with the company targeting nearly 200 km (124 miles) of range.

European versions are expected to feature 4.5 kW Type 2 AC charging, while the Chinese version will offer optional higher-power DC fast charging. The bike rolls on 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheels wearing Michelin City Grip tires, and riders get a 10.25-inch TFT display along with an optional 55-liter electrically operated top box.

Interestingly, the X Cruiser also incorporates certain two-wheeler intellectual property and know-how licensed from BMW Group, though Segway stresses that it is responsible for the vehicle’s development, integration, validation, production and certification.

The X Cruiser may be the weirdest – and thus perhaps the most interesting – of Segway’s EICMA debuts, but it was far from alone.

The company also unveiled the Segway Orca Concept, a futuristic high-performance electric maxi-scooter concept built around an 800V electrical architecture and a nearly 20 kWh battery.

Segway is targeting up to 300 km (186 miles) of range, a 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) time of 4.5 seconds, and the ability to add 200 km (124 miles) of range in 20 minutes. The concept also features front and rear multi-link suspension, electronically controlled multi-mode damping and a battery-integrated CTB chassis. Those figures are engineering targets rather than promised production specifications, and Segway currently describes the Orca strictly as a concept.

Its a BMW C1 reborn as electric! They were a bit of a cult thing, but underpowered for the weight. Never made it to the USA.

The biggest benefit is not really safety, its comfort.

Then there’s Segway’s expanding X Series, which moves the focus away from urban riding and toward dirt. The lineup includes the Xaber X1000 and Xaber 350, along with different Xaber 300 variants for the US and European markets. Segway is also partnering with Michelin for its Dakar Rally Factory Team, using the brutal rally environment as a real-world development and validation platform for electric off-road motorcycles.

Taken together, it’s quite the showing from a company whose name many people still associate primarily with those funny two-wheeled self-balancing machines from the early 2000s.

Segway has already expanded heavily into electric scooters, e-bikes, go-karts and powersports vehicles. Now it seems increasingly serious about becoming an electric motorcycle company as well.

And if motorcycles with roll cages, roofs and seatbelts are part of that future, things could get pretty interesting… pretty quickly!

#5150. Canada’s National Bank Discloses XRP Position Through Bitwise

Despite the slowed performance witnessed across the XRP ETF market in recent weeks, it appears that interest in the investment product remains intact especially through its largest issuer, Bitwise.

In a recent 13F filings with the U.S. SEC, the national bank of Canada, revealed it recently joined the XRP ETF ecosystem, showcasing its exposure to XRP through the Bitwise XRP ETF.

Although the bank did not disclose the specific amount it had invested in the asset, the filing has triggered discussions as it highlights XRP’s growing exposure among institutional investors.

Notably, the Form 13F the bank filed with the SEC covers the third quarter of 2026, which ended on September 30. This suggests that it had recently joined the XRP ecosystem despite the prolonged market weakness.

Unlike regular investors who purchase XRP directly from exchanges and hold in their wallets, the bank invested in XRP through Bitwise's fund.

With its XRP ETF offering, Bitwise allows traditional investors to gain exposure to XRP without having to manage the crypto asset themselves.

Although XRP has continued to see major institutions and banks join its ETF ecosystem, participation in the XRP funds have slowed significantly following the ongoing market volatility.

While the exposure showcased by the major Canadian bank shows growing XRP ETF adoption, it doesn’t change the fact that institutional traders are beginning to take caution as they have just recorded the highest weekly withdrawals since March 2026.

The bank’s XRP exposure has triggered discussions as it shows that it has retained its position till September 30 despite the persisting market correction.

#5149. BYD’s newest EV is about as big as a Toyota Camry, but brings a lot more tech for $23K

BYD launched the new Seal 07 in China, where it starts at around $23,000. It’s about the size of a Toyota Camry, but brings a surprising amount of tech and premium features for the money.

After introducing the updated first-generation Seal 07 in March, BYD launched the second-gen model on Thursday.

The second-generation Seal 07, which BYD calls the “new choice for a class-leading luxury experience,” is available in battery electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains.

BYD offers five variants, including two PHEVs and three EVs, starting at 139,900 yuan (about $21,000) for the plug-in hybrid and 149,900 yuan (around $22,500) for the fully electric version.

The new Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery, providing a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).

It comes standard with a single rear-mounted electric motor producing up to 328 hp (245 kW) and 269 lb-ft (365 Nm) of torque, which BYD says enables it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 5.5 seconds.

All plug-in hybrid variants use BYD’s latest DM-i system, which features a 1.5L turbocharged engine with 154 hp (115 kW) and a 214 hp (160 kW) front electric motor.

The new Seal 07 PHEV has a smaller 37 kWh battery that provides up to 205 miles (330 km) of pure electric CLTC range. That’s a considerable jump from the 143 miles (230 km) of electric range the previous generation offered.

Thanks to BYD’s latest Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

Both versions are 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm tall, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly bigger than the Toyota Camry.

Inside, the new Seal 07 adopts BYD’s latest cabin design, including a 15.6″ floating center infotainment screen, a 10.25″ instrument cluster, and two rear passenger entertainment screens.

BYD added several premium extras, including a built-in 6.8L smart refrigerator, zero gravity seats, and driver headrest audio. It also offers the most rear passenger space and the largest frunk (160L) in its class, according to BYD.

The Seal 07 debuts BYD’s Smart Ecosystem 2.0, including “Diva,” a smartwatch that can interact with the vehicle and let drivers manage functions remotely.

Higher-priced models offer BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driving system, with a roof-mounted LiDAR available as an option. The setup provides safety and convenience features such as Navigation on Autopilot in the city and on highways, plus full-scenario intelligent parking.

BYD is offering a limited-time “Super trade-in price” promo, starting at 145,900 yuan ($22,000) for the new Seal 07 EV and 135,900 yuan ($20,500) for the PHEV version.

Fundstrat co-founder and BitMine chairman Tom Lee expects the price of Ethereum to bottom shortly before the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic. "If ETH follows the same path as the SPCX IPO, ETH bottoms shortly before the ANT IPO," Lee wrote on X.

Lee shared a Bloomberg and Fundstrat chart that compares the price of ETH ahead of the SpaceX IPO in June with the current decline. According to the chart, ETH lost 39% over eight weeks before the SpaceX offering, including 29% in the final two weeks. Ahead of the Anthropic IPO, ETH has also lost 39% over two months, including 28% in the last two weeks.

If ETH follows same path as SPCX IPO, $ETH bottoms shortly before $ANT IPO https://t.co/FS6T3KiRpo

SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO in June. The bottom for ETH came three trading days before SpaceX priced its shares, and the price of ETH went up after that.

Anthropic is set to price its IPO on Nov. 18 and aims to raise up to $64.4 billion. It would be the second-largest IPO in history after SpaceX.

Lee blamed the decline of ETH on a rotation of money into the Anthropic IPO, and Binance founder Changpeng Zhao and Strive CEO Matt Cole have pointed to the same flow of liquidity. On Monday, ETH is trading at $1,823.

BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), which Lee chairs, has bought ETH every week since it launched its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025. In its Nov. 16 update, the company disclosed fresh numbers: it added 7,653 ETH to its reserves last week and 9,587 ETH the week before.

BitMine now holds 6,077,745 ETH, or 4.97% of all coins in circulation (about 122.2 million ETH), and it is the world's largest corporate Ethereum treasury. According to the company, it is 99% of the way through its "Alchemy of 5%" program, and fewer than 35,000 ETH are left to reach the target.

The total portfolio of BitMine, which includes crypto, cash, securities and venture stakes, has shrunk from a peak of more than $14 billion to $11.8 billion. According to BitMine, 5,227,037 ETH, or around 86% of the reserve, is staked.

Lee expects the growth cycle for ETH to last two to three years, driven by bank tokenization, and his base-case targets for ETH range from $12,000 to $22,000.

#5145. 178 Websites Infected in Major Optimizely Hack: Crypto Wallets Targeted, but Bitcoin Barely Reacted

Optimizely attack infects 178 websites, steals crypto and card data, and exposes users to wallet-address swaps and iPhone exploits.

An Optimizely attack on Monday, November 16, planted crypto-stealing code on the websites of 178 organizations, including Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN. The malicious script swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed card numbers, and tried to break into iPhones for about 19 hours before it was cleaned up.

BREAKING: A cyberattack hit 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA and Air France-KLM, by loading malware on the Optimizely Web platform, exposing visitors to scripts built to steal payment data and exploit iOS…

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) November 17, 2026

Optimizely is a tool companies use to test different versions of their web pages. An attacker slipped code into the scripts it serves, so every site that loaded them ran the malware.

We traced the attacker’s Bitcoin wallet. It received five payments worth about $5,500, and one victim alone sent nearly 90% of it. Bitcoin barely moved while the attack ran.

So what happened, and what is the real impact of hacks like this one?

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the code and published a full breakdown. The attacker wrote it into a settings field in customers’ Optimizely projects, so it was served from Optimizely’s own servers and looked legitimate.

Optimizely said it “secured affected user accounts and added protections against further unauthorized code delivery.” Report URI found no sign that Ledger hardware wallets themselves were breached. The danger was on the website, where a copied address could be swapped before a user pasted it.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

Report URI listed the attacker’s wallets. We checked the Bitcoin one on mempool.space, the public Bitcoin block explorer.

The Optimizely attack’s impact was tiny, and the market ignored it. Bitcoin is near $64,300 after its weekend low of $62,006, and that slide came from wider selling, not this attack.

EXPLORE: Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 Billion in 2026, More Than Triple 2025: How Did Bitcoin and Ether React?

The money stolen in the Optimizely attack is small, but the method is the year’s most damaging one. We sorted DefiLlama’s 2026 hack list by attack type. Attacks on websites and infrastructure, rather than on smart contracts, are now the costliest category:

These attacks hit users where no wallet setting can protect them. The fix is on the user’s side: check the address on the hardware wallet’s screen before signing, send a small test transfer first, and keep phones updated.

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $64,326. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $76,208, and its 200-day EMA at $75,864.

The Optimizely attack did not move Bitcoin, and the attacker walked away with about $7,000. Its real cost is trust: when a hardware-wallet maker’s own website can serve malware for hours, checking every address on the device is no longer optional.

XRP's weekly momentum remains weak, with $0.84 emerging as critical trendline support; reclaiming $1.12 could strengthen the recovery.

XRP Ledger active users surge, while futures open interest drops, highlighting a growing disconnect between network activity and market participation.

The broader crypto market is still struggling to find its footing after the recent sell-off, leaving investors cautious about what comes next. Bitcoin’s attempts to recover have yet to bring much confidence back into the altcoin market, and XRP is no exception. The token has managed to climb back above $1 after slipping below $0.90, offering some relief to buyers. However, the recovery is still fragile, particularly as the broader market continues to face selling pressure.

Interestingly, XRP’s price isn’t the only thing worth watching right now. Activity on the XRP Ledger has been picking up even as the token struggles to build a sustained recovery. This contrast adds another dimension to the current market setup. Is XRP simply caught in the broader market weakness, or are there signs of a shift beneath the surface? Its price action over the coming sessions could offer some clues.

XRP’s weekly chart continues to favour the bears, with the token struggling to recover after its sharp decline from the $3.50 peak in 2025. The recent selling has pushed the price back towards $1, and buyers are yet to show enough strength to turn the trend around. Although XRP has managed to stay close to this psychological level, the broader chart suggests that the recovery remains uncertain.

The weekly RSI is at 36.05, sitting below its moving average of 48.43, while the CMF remains negative at -0.12. Both readings point to continued weakness, with buying pressure yet to make a meaningful comeback. The RSI is approaching oversold territory, but it hasn’t dropped below 30, leaving room for further weakness.

One level that could become particularly important is the ascending trendline near $0.84. It has supported XRP through several major corrections since 2022, making it an important level for buyers to defend. If the price holds above this trendline, it could give bulls some breathing room to attempt a recovery.

However, a weekly close below it would weaken the longer-term structure and bring the $0.55 region back into focus. For now, reclaiming $1 is the immediate challenge, followed by the $1.10 to $1.20 resistance zone. Until XRP clears these levels, any recovery attempt could face seller resistance.

XRP is showing two very different trends beneath the surface. While participation across the derivatives market has dropped considerably, activity on the XRP Ledger has been moving higher. This contrast is particularly interesting given that XRP’s price continues to struggle near $1.

Data from CoinGlass shows that XRP futures open interest fell from about $3.4 billion on October 8 to around $1.9 billion by November 18. That’s a contraction of roughly 44% in just over a month. The decline suggests that traders have been reducing their exposure, with a significant amount of leveraged positioning being unwound during the recent price weakness. The picture looks quite different on the network side.

According to Token Terminal, daily active users on the XRP Ledger have climbed to 48,400 as of November 18. The metric largely fluctuated between 15,000 and 20,000 during August and September before picking up through October and accelerating further in November. This suggests that engagement across the network has increased even as XRP’s market performance has weakened.

The divergence raises an interesting question about what is driving the increase in network activity and whether it can eventually translate into stronger demand for XRP. For now, the two metrics point to a market where network engagement is improving, but speculative interest remains subdued.

XRP’s recovery is still facing an important test. The token needs to hold above key support levels and attract stronger buying interest if it is to move out of its current downtrend. For now, the $0.84 trendline remains an important level to watch, while a move above 1.10–1.20 could give buyers some confidence that the recovery is gaining strength.

There are also some interesting developments beneath the surface. While futures traders have been pulling back, activity on the XRP Ledger has picked up considerably. Whether this growing network engagement will eventually translate into stronger demand for XRP remains to be seen. Until buyers return in greater numbers and the price starts reclaiming important resistance levels, a sustained recovery may remain difficult. For the XRP price, the next move will depend on whether improving network activity can finally find support in the market.

#5143. Nvidia and IBM’s 13,000x Quantum Speedup Raises New ‘Q-Day’ Questions for Bitcoin

Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab announced new tools for quantum error correction on Nov. 16, and the news comes amid a debate in the crypto industry about "Q-Day," the moment when a quantum computer will be able to break Bitcoin's cryptography. As of Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $64,580.

Nvidia released a new decoding algorithm, TCBP-JOBS, on Nov. 16. According to the company, the algorithm delivers up to 13,000x faster decoding compared with existing leading algorithms, and it cuts the computation time for researching new quantum computing designs from 12 weeks to 45 minutes.

Nvidia said that the algorithm helps researchers find designs that use physical qubits more efficiently, "shortening the path to practical fault-tolerant quantum computing."

Nvidia and IBM also announced plans for a modular quantum computing codesign platform with Fermilab. IBM and Nvidia are placing Nvidia DGX B200 systems next to IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and researchers will use the platform to develop and test error-correction codes.

"Making quantum computers useful for science requires advances in error correction, applications and the systems that bring quantum processors and accelerated computing together," said Krysta Svore, vice president of applied research for quantum computing at Nvidia.

A 2022 study by researchers from the University of Sussex estimated that breaking Bitcoin's encryption within a day would require around 13 million physical qubits.

IBM Quantum Nighthawk, which IBM calls its fastest quantum processor, has 120 qubits. According to Nvidia, errors in quantum processors "limit the complexity and duration of the computations they can perform."

In 2024, Bitcoin developer Hunter Beast proposed BIP-360, a new output type that would protect coins from quantum attacks. In July 2025, Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp also suggested a plan to phase out legacy signatures and move coins to quantum-resistant addresses.

Early coins mined by Satoshi Nakamoto sit on addresses with public keys that are already visible on the blockchain.

In November 2024, NIST proposed to stop allowing vulnerable public-key algorithms, including elliptic curve cryptography, after 2035.

#5141. Harvard Refuses to Dump Bitcoin Holdings Despite Downturn

Elite university Harvard maintains significant Bitcoin exposure as it holds over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin ETF, a recent regulatory filing has revealed.

Harvard University remains highly exposed to Bitcoin (BTC) as the elite institution continues to hold over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF).

As per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Company, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

The Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

As per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

For instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

Later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

During the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

Since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Harvard University is not the only top-tier American university that has gained exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market capitalization.

In October 2024, Emory University became the first U.S. university endowment to publicly disclose its holdings in a Bitcoin ETF.

It held roughly 2.7 million shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust, worth over $15 million at the time.

Meanwhile, in May 2025, Brown University disclosed its holdings of 105,000 shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth roughly $4.9 million as of March 31 of that year.

Later, Brown doubled its stake, bringing its holdings to 212,500 shares.

Meanwhile, Dartmouth College has also joined the list of universities with exposure to cryptocurrency ETFs.

In its recent filing, Dartmouth College disclosed that it held 201,531 IBIT shares. The investment was worth roughly $9.5 million as of the end of September 2026.

The last time the ETFs turned green, on November 4, the next day brought $430 million of outflows and a 5.5% drop. So is Monday a turning point for BTC, or are more tests coming?

#5137. Ripple's Schwartz Reveals Why XRP Ledger Used Satoshi's Code

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

In his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz said they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet said that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

Some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating new ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," said Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a new cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz said it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

"It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz said.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.
