#5136. Tesla wants its sworn Cybercab answers to NHTSA kept entirely secret

Tesla has answered NHTSA’s Special Order demanding it prove, under oath, that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The response landed on the October 30 deadline, and Tesla asked the agency to keep all of it confidential.

The only part of the filing the public can read is a 30-page guide for firefighters. Everything about how a car with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors was certified as compliant is blacked out.

We reported in September that NHTSA had ordered Tesla to show its work on the Cybercab’s certification. The order came one week after the company started charging for Cybercab rides in Austin on September 3 and put 21 questions to the company, with civil penalties of up to $139 million for an incomplete answer and criminal exposure for a false one.

Tesla first tried to buy time. On September 18, it asked for eight more weeks, until November 20, citing “the voluminous nature of the request” and the work of searching its records and writing “thorough narrative formats in response to each question.” NHTSA gave it 30 days instead. The new deadline was October 30, and Tesla met it.

Three Tesla documents now sit in the AQ26002 docket, and two of them are empty.

The first is Tesla’s response letter, dated October 30 and addressed from 1 Tesla Road in Austin. It is one page long. The only text is: “The entirety of this file is confidential business information.”

The second is a placeholder for Tesla’s answer to Request 8, which asked the company to explain, standard by standard, how it determined the Cybercab complies: which subpart it certified to, and whether it ran physical tests, simulations, or engineering analyses. Per NHTSA’s note, the responsive documents carry a confidentiality request “for the entirety of each document.”

The third is the only substantive document: Tesla’s Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan, version 1.2, dated September 3. It’s a real document with useful information in it. It’s also something Tesla has had on its website since July, aimed at police and fire crews, not regulators.

So the public gets a tow-truck manual, and the certification argument stays sealed.

The Special Order wasn’t a fishing expedition. It named the rules the Cybercab doesn’t obviously meet, and it seeks to understand how Tesla believes it can get around it.

FMVSS 135 says “the service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control.” NHTSA has stated in public that a manufacturer of a vehicle with no foot brake can’t certify to it, then asked Tesla how it did. FMVSS 108 requires a turn-signal control that cancels itself when the steering wheel turns. FMVSS 111 requires mirrors. And the agency wanted to know whether Tesla certified the car with temporary driver controls bolted in and then removed them, which would run into the Safety Act’s “make inoperative” prohibition.

It also asked how the Cybercab is legal without a Part 555 exemption, the route Amazon’s Zoox took for its own steering-wheel-less robotaxi in July. Zoox applied, made its case, and got an exemption capped at 2,500 vehicles a year. Tesla self-certified and started charging for rides.

Every one of those answers is now under a confidentiality claim.

The first-responder plan was written for a different audience, but it brushes against several of NHTSA’s questions.

It says the Cybercab is “not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals.” The word “typically” is doing work there. The same document notes that a Cybercab with a steering wheel and pedals “is typically an engineering or test vehicle, and operates at SAE Level 2 autonomy,” and includes instructions for driving one. That’s relevant to Requests 5 through 7, which asked whether the subject vehicles can be driven with temporarily attached controls.

It describes an operational design domain covering “all public roadways, such as freeways, highways, city streets, and rural roads,” at all hours, in light and moderate rain, fog, and snow. That is a far wider envelope than the Austin geofence the cars run in today, and it references an “Arizona Areas of Operation Appendix.” Request 1 asked for the ODD and Request 2 for scaling plans.

And it confirms that first responders can be granted access to on-board touchscreen controls to move the car, after showing a badge to the B-pillar camera (that’s interesting). Request 20 asked whether the touchscreen can move the vehicle and under what restrictions.

Nothing in it touches brakes, mirrors, telltales, or the certification itself.

Confidentiality requests go to NHTSA’s Chief Counsel under Part 512. The agency decides whether Tesla’s claim holds, and it can order a public version released if it doesn’t. NHTSA hasn’t said anything about the request, and it hasn’t found the Cybercab noncompliant with any standard.

This is familiar. In June 2025, Tesla asked NHTSA to hide its answers about the original Robotaxi launch in Austin, a service running on supervised FSD while FSD was under investigation. Those answers never surfaced.

NHTSA’s opening resume for the audit put the affected population at about 1,000 vehicles. The Cybercab is still carrying passengers in Austin while the agency reads a filing nobody else can.

I don't see how the answers can have confidential business secrets. It is about meeting public safety standards, not asking for schematics, technical details or designs. It is about clear public safety requirement and how the vehicle qualify as meeting it.

The so called keyword from Tesla's self certification is "applicable". Tesla may argue that many of those requirements aren't applicable in their test vehicle. But I would like to see the justifications on that.

Tesla’s position in September was that the Cybercab complies with every applicable federal standard, including the one that requires a brake pedal. If that’s true, the argument for it is the most interesting document in the autonomous vehicle industry right now, and Tesla just asked the government to make sure nobody reads it.

We get why a company redacts test data and supplier details. But the legal theory for how a car with no foot brake meets a foot-brake rule doesn’t sound like a trade secret to me. Zoox’s exemption petition is public. Waymo’s safety framework is public. Tesla’s case for why it didn’t need to ask is sealed, cover letter included.

NHTSA now has to decide whether “the entirety of this file” is really confidential business information. If it says no, we’ll finally see how Tesla certified this car. If it says yes, about 1,000 Cybercabs keep driving on a certification the public isn’t allowed to check.

Investors who miss out on Anthropic’s IPO, set for Thursday, may still end up owning a small piece of the AI company through funds they already hold. Many actively managed mutual funds and ETFs bought Anthropic shares before the listing, so investors in those funds will gain exposure automatically once trading begins. Index funds will add the stock over the following weeks, though timing varies. Inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 and Russell 3000 is expected to take longer than it did for SpaceX. In most funds, Anthropic will make up well under 1% of holdings, which limits the impact of any sharp price swings after the debut. In an interview with CNBC, Jay Ritter, director of the IPO Initiative at the University of Florida, cautioned against putting too much money into any single stock. Anthropic could raise up to about $90 billion including its private placement, which would top SpaceX’s $86 billion record from June. The listing comes amid wider doubts about the AI trade after Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia.

#5133. XRP Price Near Crucial Support That Could Trigger $3.50 Bull Run

XRP price could bottom out at $0.78, according to analyst Ali Martinez.

In a recent post on X, Martinez shared a chart with what appears to be an ascending triangle pattern. The triangle's closest low is at $0.78.

XRP has already fallen 43% from its October high of $1.55. According to Martinez, the correction might continue until the price reaches the bottom.

If the price holds $0.78, a possible bull run toward $3.50 might follow.

"A weekly breakout above $3.50, followed by a successful retest as support, could confirm the multi-year ascending triangle and trigger a bull run to $18," Martinez wrote.

On the weekend, XRP price recovered 7% from its previous crash, but couldn't reach the $1 level.

The RSI fell below 25 before the latest recovery, which suggests oversold conditions.

A rebound following a massive sell-off does not equal a trend reversal.

In October, the 200 EMA acted as strong resistance that XRP was unable to break.The $1 mark is the first psychological threshold XRP needs to reclaim, acting as both support and resistance.

The $1.3 level is where the breakdown started and where volatility spiked. The 200 EMA sits near $1.33 right now.

A ransomware group called The Gentlemen has claimed it breached Nvidia, adding the chipmaker to its dark web leak site with a “SOON” label and a countdown of about 10 days, according to cybersecurity news account International Cyber Digest. The listing does not yet include any stolen files, and there is no public evidence so far that Nvidia’s data has been taken. Nvidia has not confirmed any breach. The Gentlemen operates a ransomware-as-a-service model, renting its tools to other hackers, and says it has hit more than 1,000 victims across many countries and industries. Ransomware groups often use countdown timers to pressure companies into paying before data is released, and some claims later prove exaggerated or false. The report comes a day after Nvidia beat earnings forecasts in its first results since Jensen Huang’s resignation, and follows a week of security incidents involving TSMC employee data and a reported attack through web platform Optimizely.

#5130. BTC Price Drops 15% as Gold and Silver Dump: Can December’s Fed Decision Turn It?

BTC price fell 15% since Nov 5, more than gold and silver, as a December Fed hike nears 95% odds. Could this shift price action?

Gold (XAU) fell 2.5% to about $3,770 an ounce on Wednesday, November 18, as traders bet on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Silver dropped 3.3% to $45.70. Both metals are at their lowest since September 2025. The BTC price held near $64,600, but it has fallen even harder than the metals since the hike bets took off.

Gold prices sink beneath $3,800, hitting a 14-month low as the hawkish Fed outlook and firm dollar weigh on bullion – FX

— First Squawk (@FirstSquawk) November 18, 2026

We compared the moves since November 5, the day before a strong October jobs report changed the rate outlook. Bitcoin is down 15%, silver 12.5% and gold 8.4%. Over the same days, the U.S. dollar index rose 2.2%, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed from 4.84% to 5.10%.

Higher rates hit everything that pays no interest, and gold, silver and bitcoin all fall into that group. So the next big test is the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting.

Gold peaked near $5,320 an ounce on COMEX futures in late January. It has since lost 29%, and silver has lost 60% from its January high of $115. On Monday, gold for immediate delivery touched $3,832, and Wednesday’s drop pushed it lower still.

The reason is the Fed. Markets now treat another hike as almost certain:

A quarter-point hike would lift the Fed’s target range to 4.00%-4.25%. It would be the second this year, after September’s. Waller has gone further, saying a half-point move, or “a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered.”

Central banks are still buying gold, 675 tonnes in the first nine months of the year. That hasn’t been enough to offset a stronger dollar and higher yields.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Some investors call bitcoin “digital gold,” but in this selloff the BTC price hasn’t acted as a hedge.

We matched daily moves over the last 15 gold trading sessions, from October 29 to November 18:

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index sits at 11, deep in “extreme fear,” just above the weekend’s low of 10.

EXPLORE: Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

With a quarter-point hike at 95%, that move is largely expected already. For the BTC price, the surprise would be a bigger move or a pause:

The minutes of the October meeting come out today at 2 p.m. ET and could move the odds before December. In October, two officials, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted to hike when the rest voted to hold.

The BTC price stands at $64,590 on Binance, down 48% from its October 2025 record. On the daily chart, it sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,780, and its 200-day EMA at $75,760.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

Gold, silver and bitcoin are all trading as bets on the Fed right now. Until December 9, the BTC price is likely to keep moving with yields and the dollar, not against them.

#5129. Shiba Inu (SHIB) Bearish Rally is Fading, Solana (SOL) Death Cross Isn't Dangerous, Stellar (XLM) Recovery Signal Potential: Crypto Market Review

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The crypto market remains under pressure, with Bitcoin dropping to a four-month low around $62,000 on November 15. SHIB, SOL and XLM all printed new lows on November 14, yet selling volume stayed well below earlier spikes, and oversold RSI readings suggest a recovery could be near, even though fundamental catalysts are still missing.

Thankfully, Shiba Inu's bearish rally might be fading sooner rather than later. The price's most recent red candle wasn't followed by a surge in selling volume, which could hint at a potential reversal.

On November 14, a single daily candle took SHIB below the July bottom around $0.0000041, with the wick reaching $0.0000037. At press time, the asset is trading at $0.00000387, the lowest level on the chart since March. Selling volume that day stayed well below the late July and August spikes.

Usually, when the price hits the bottom like that, the point of previously growing demand might become a source of additional selling pressure. For SHIB, it's the July zone, where buyers stepped in last time.

If we dive inside the 4HR price chart, we can clearly see a price/volume divergence, which is a good sign for bulls. Moving averages are diverging, so a quick retrace isn't yet possible. There's also potential for a quicker recovery thanks to RSI, which is sitting in the oversold zone on the daily chart.

SHIB is trading below all of its moving averages, with the 200 EMA hanging at around $0.0000054. Bitcoin's drop to a four-month low around $62,000 on November 15 didn't help either.

Despite the death cross on the chart solidifying, there's a good chance it's not critical. The price is showing negative performance one way or another, but it's not going to add more fuel to the bearish furnace.

The cross formed near $96, where a shorter moving average dropped below the 200 EMA, and another moving average is about to follow. SOL is trading at $71.70 after a wick to around $67.50 on November 14. Since its late September peak near $125, Solana has lost over 40% of its value.

First of all, death crosses aren't as scary as they used to be. Second, the signal is inherently lagging, so it only reflects what was already priced in. It's more of a guideline for those who are looking for an entry.

The chart shows a negative dynamic indeed, but, in a similar fashion to Shiba Inu, the bearish rally printed the first descending volume bar in a long time. Though it's only a single candle, it might be the start of a recovery.

The price is already oversold, but the bottom might be closer to $62, which is also reinforced by RSI. Back in June, $62 was the point where SOL bottomed out before the summer recovery.

Stellar has reached a potential price bottom where it might finally find ground for a retrace. The volume is relatively low, but the main issue is the lack of foundational recovery fuel.

XLM is trading at $0.1384 after dropping to $0.13 on November 14. That's below the May low around $0.142, the zone from which XLM spiked toward $0.30 in June. The RSI dipped below 30 during the drop. Since the late September high near $0.235, XLM has lost around 40%, while selling volume stayed far below the June and July spikes.

Short-term moving averages are crossing longer-term moving averages, and the issue here is that it's a signal of short-term aggravation. All of them are now above the price, with the 200 EMA at around $0.184.

The XLM update coming on November 23 is most likely priced in and unlikely to change the price direction fundamentally. Protocol 30, codenamed Bell, goes to a mainnet validator vote that day.

It adds post-quantum signature checks and muxed addresses for Soroban smart contracts and prepares the network for faster ledger timing. The upgrade has already been live on testnet since early November.

The key here is the crypto market recovery in general.

#5127. Mastercard Spotlights XRP Ledger After Groundbreaking Test

After an important hackathon that demonstrated how AI agents could autonomously perform payments using blockchain, global payments giant Mastercard has spotlighted the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

36 hours. 179 hackers. 70 submissions. At the XRP Ledger Hackathon, developers used Mastercard Agent Pay for machines to explore new possibilities for micropayments and autonomous commerce, including how AI agents can transact within defined spending limits and with verified merchants. See what we learned about the future of agentic commerce: https://t.co/S4NwQxxuRi #AgenticCommerce #DigitalAssets #AI

Global payments giant Mastercard recently posted on X about the outcome of the XRP Ledger Hackathon. In the post, the payments firm detailed that 179 developers submitted 70 projects during the 36-hour event in Manhattan.

The focus of the competition was how to enable AI-powered agents to autonomously execute transactions and micropayments, engage with verified merchants and so forth, all while operating within budgets set by developers.

The hackathon was held as part of the preparations for Ripple’s annual conference called Swell. Mastercard, Amazon Web Services, QuickNode and Ledger supported the event, which had a prize pool of over $40,000.

Mastercard published an official article in which it mentioned the challenge given to developers. They had to build AI agents that could autonomously make payments to verified merchants without human input.

Also, the agents had to operate within a specified budget. They had to settle payments using Ripple’s USD-backed stablecoin called RLUSD. They had to do this on the XRP Ledger.

One of the purposes of the challenge was to showcase how blockchain infrastructure can enable micropayments. This is especially the case for micropayments smaller than one cent.

In the future, these micropayments could be valuable as AI agents start buying computational resources or requesting data from other AI agents and then making payments themselves for digital services.

Mastercard’s vice president of digital assets, Michael Broderick, stressed that the company's technology called Agent Pay for Machines could enable such payments.

One of the most interesting things mentioned in the Mastercard report might be how the XRP Ledger is increasingly being used for payments by machines.

Mastercard mentioned that over 500,000 transactions are being conducted daily on the XRPL by AI agents.

Also, it’s reported that Ripple has recorded over 10 million payments using the x402 internet payment protocol on XRPL. This comes less than three months after the protocol crossed the 1 million payment milestone on the network.
